What is the difference between <main> and <body>?
body: <main> holds the primary content, <body> contains everything visible in the page.

title: What is the use of <nav> tag?
body: It defines navigation links.

title: What is the difference between inline, internal, and external CSS in HTML?
body: Inline is inside a tag, internal inside <style>, external via <link>.

title: What is the difference between <link> and <a> tag?
body: <link> is for resources (CSS, favicon), <a> creates hyperlinks.

title: What is the difference between id and class in HTML?
body: Id is unique for one element, class can be shared by multiple elements.

title: What is the difference between relative, absolute, and fixed paths for links?
body: Relative is based on current file, absolute is full URL, fixed path is from root.

title: What is the difference between <script> in <head> and at end of <body>?
body: In <head> it loads before content (can block rendering), in <body> it loads after content.

title: What is the difference between <noscript> and <script>?
body: <noscript> defines content shown if JavaScript is disabled.

title: What is the difference between defer and async in <script>?
body: async loads script while parsing, defer runs after HTML is parsed.

title: What is the difference between inline elements and block-level elements in HTML5?
body: Block takes full width (e.g., <div>), inline fits only content (e.g., <span>).

title: What is the difference between <em> and <mark>?
body: <em> emphasizes text, <mark> highlights text.

title: What is the difference between <small> and <sub>?
body: <small> reduces font size, <sub> makes text subscript.

title: What is the difference between <abbr> and <acronym>?
body: <abbr> defines an abbreviation with title, <acronym> is obsolete in HTML5.

title: What is the difference between <u> and <ins>?
body: <u> underlines text visually, <ins> represents inserted text semantically.

title: What is the difference between <bdo> and <bdi>?
body: <bdo> overrides text direction, <bdi> isolates bidirectional text.

title: What is the difference between <meta charset="UTF-8"> and <meta http-equiv>?
body: charset defines character encoding, http-equiv sets HTTP header-like metadata.

title: What is the difference between viewport meta tag and responsive design?
body: Viewport meta controls scaling, responsive design adapts layout via CSS.

title: What is the purpose of alt and title attributes in images?
body: alt is for accessibility/SEO, title shows tooltip on hover.

title: What is the difference between inline SVG and ?
body: Inline SVG allows styling and scripting, is just an image reference.

title: What is the difference between <video> controls and <audio> controls?
body: Both add media players, <video> shows visual controls, <audio> has sound-only.

title: What is the difference between <canvas> and <svg>?
body: <canvas> is pixel-based drawing, <svg> is vector-based graphics.

title: What is the difference between <source> and <track> in media tags?
body: <source> specifies media files, <track> adds captions/subtitles.

title: What is the difference between GET and POST in HTML forms?
body: GET appends data in URL, POST sends in request body.

title: What is the difference between action and method in forms?
body: action specifies where data goes, method specifies how (GET/POST).

title: What is the difference between name and id attributes in forms?
body: name is for form submission, id uniquely identifies element in DOM.

title: What is the difference between required and pattern attributes?
body: required makes a field mandatory, pattern enforces regex format.

title: What is the difference between disabled and readonly in inputs?
body: disabled field cannot be edited or submitted, readonly is not editable but submitted.

title: What is the difference between checkbox and radio button?
body: Checkbox allows multiple selections, radio allows only one in a group.

title: What is the difference between <datalist> and <select>?
body: <datalist> gives suggestions with free typing, <select> restricts to options.

title: What is the difference between placeholder and value attributes in inputs?
body: placeholder shows hint text, value shows actual input value.

title: What is the difference between <label> with for and without for?
body: With for, label links to an input id; without, input must be nested inside label.

title: What is the difference between <fieldset> and <legend>?
body: <fieldset> groups form elements, <legend> provides a caption.

title: What is the difference between <meter> and <progress>?
body: <meter> shows a known measurement (e.g., score), <progress> shows task progress.

title: What is the difference between inline event handling and JavaScript event listeners?
body: Inline uses onclick in HTML, listeners use JavaScript’s addEventListener().

title: What is the difference between accessibility and SEO in HTML?
body: Accessibility improves usability for all users, SEO improves search ranking.

title: What is ARIA in HTML?
body: Accessible Rich Internet Applications – attributes that improve screen reader support.

title: What is the difference between aria-label and alt?
body: aria-label is for accessibility on any element, alt is specific to images.

title: What is the difference between absolute, relative, and fixed positioning in HTML/CSS?
body: Absolute positions relative to nearest ancestor, relative to itself, fixed to viewport.

title: What is the difference between inline frames and embedding with <object>?
body: <iframe> embeds another webpage, <object> can embed media, PDFs, etc.

title: What is the difference between cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage in HTML5?
body: Cookies are small server-stored data, localStorage persists, sessionStorage clears when tab closes.

title: What is the difference between HTML entities and Unicode characters?
body: Entities use &entity; (e.g., <), Unicode uses actual code points.

title: What is the difference between <base> tag and <link> tag?
body: <base> sets default URL for links, <link> references external resources.

title: What is the difference between inline styles and external stylesheets for performance?
body: Inline increases page size, external allows caching and reuse.

title: What is the difference between HTML validation and linting?
body: Validation checks HTML against W3C rules, linting checks coding style and errors.

title: What is the difference between inline HTML comments and conditional comments?
body: Inline comments <!-- comment --> hide code from rendering, conditional comments (used in old IE) apply only to specific Internet Explorer versions.

title: What is the difference between HTML and XHTML?
body: XHTML is stricter, requires proper nesting, lowercase tags, and closed elements.

title: What is the difference between HTML5 and older versions regarding doctype?
body: HTML5 uses a simple <!DOCTYPE html>, older versions had long doctypes.

title: What is the difference between quirks mode and standards mode?
body: Quirks mode emulates old browsers, standards mode follows modern HTML/CSS rules.

title: How does HTML5 improve SEO compared to HTML4?
body: Semantic tags like <article>, <section>, <nav> help search engines understand content.

title: What is the difference between microdata, RDFa, and JSON-LD?
body: All provide structured data; JSON-LD is preferred by Google, microdata is inline, RDFa uses attributes.

title: What is the difference between <meta name="keywords"> and <meta name="description">?
body: Keywords are mostly ignored by search engines, description is used in search snippets.

title: What is the difference between rel="noopener" and rel="noreferrer" in links?
body: noopener prevents window.opener access, noreferrer hides referrer information.

title: What is the difference between sandbox attribute in <iframe> and CSP?
body: Sandbox restricts iframe capabilities, CSP controls overall resource security.

title: What is the difference between progressive rendering and lazy loading?
body: Progressive rendering loads content as it arrives, lazy loading defers offscreen content.

title: What is the difference between and ?
body: <picture> gives full control for responsive images, srcset selects best resolution.

title: What is the difference between accessibility tree and DOM tree?
body: DOM is full HTML structure, accessibility tree is simplified view for assistive tech.

title: What is the difference between aria-hidden="true" and hidden attribute?
body: aria-hidden hides from screen readers only, hidden hides from all users.

title: What is the difference between Shadow DOM and regular DOM?
body: Shadow DOM encapsulates styles/components, regular DOM is global.

title: What is the difference between <slot> in web components and <template>?
body: <slot> is a placeholder in Shadow DOM, <template> defines reusable HTML fragments.

title: What is the difference between <noscript> and feature detection in JS?
body: <noscript> shows fallback when JS is disabled, feature detection adapts dynamically.

title: What is the difference between WebSockets and Server-Sent Events in HTML5?
body: WebSockets allow bidirectional communication, SSE is one-way server → client.

title: What is the difference between <progress> max value and <meter> value range?
body: <progress> shows task completion up to max, <meter> represents a bounded measurement.

title: What is the difference between contenteditable attribute and textarea?
body: contenteditable allows inline editing of any element, <textarea> is a form field.

title: What is the difference between autofocus and tabindex attributes?
body: autofocus gives focus on load, tabindex controls tab order navigation.

title: What is the difference between passive event listeners and regular ones in HTML5?
body: Passive listeners improve scroll performance by preventing default blocking.

title: What is the difference between preloading and prefetching in HTML?
body: Preload fetches resources needed soon, prefetch fetches resources likely needed later.

title: What is the difference between defer and module type in scripts?
body: defer runs after parsing, type="module" also supports import/export.

title: What is the difference between crossorigin attribute in images and scripts?
body: It enables CORS requests for external resources like fonts, images, scripts.

title: What is the difference between HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 in terms of HTML rendering?
body: HTTP/2 allows multiplexing, faster loading, fewer <link> hacks.

title: What is the difference between cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, and IndexedDB?
body: Cookies store small data with server access, localStorage persists, sessionStorage clears per tab, IndexedDB is large structured storage.

title: What is the difference between service workers and web workers?
body: Service workers run in background, handle caching/offline, web workers run parallel tasks.

title: What is the difference between manifest.json in PWA and cache storage?
body: Manifest defines app metadata, cache storage handles offline assets.

title: What is the difference between semantic HTML and ARIA roles?
body: Semantic HTML is built-in meaning, ARIA roles extend accessibility when semantics aren’t enough.

title: What is the difference between intrinsic and extrinsic sizing in HTML elements?
body: Intrinsic is based on content size, extrinsic is based on CSS/layout constraints.

title: What is the difference between stacking context and z-index in HTML/CSS?
body: Stacking context is a hierarchy of elements, z-index works only within its context.

title: What is the difference between DOMContentLoaded and load event?
body: DOMContentLoaded fires after HTML parsing, load fires after all resources load.

title: What is the difference between Critical Rendering Path and Repaint/Reflow?
body: CRP is the steps browser takes to render, repaint is visual update, reflow recalculates layout.

title: What is the difference between inline scripts blocking vs async scripts?
body: Inline and sync scripts block parsing, async scripts load in parallel.

title: What is the difference between FOUC and FOIT in HTML rendering?
body: FOUC = Flash of Unstyled Content, FOIT = Flash of Invisible Text (fonts).

title: What is the difference between DNS prefetch and preconnect?
body: DNS-prefetch resolves domain, preconnect establishes early TCP/SSL.

title: What is the difference between link rel="canonical" and rel="alternate"?
body: Canonical specifies preferred URL, alternate is for translations or AMP pages.

title: What is the difference between AMP HTML and regular HTML?
body: AMP is a restricted, optimized HTML for faster loading on mobile.

title: What is the difference between hydration in SSR and static HTML rendering?
body: Hydration attaches JS to server-rendered HTML, static HTML has no interactivity.

title: What is the difference between CSP script-src 'self' and 'unsafe-inline'?
body: 'self' allows only same-origin scripts, 'unsafe-inline' allows inline scripts (less secure).

title: What is the difference between rel="preload" and rel="dns-prefetch"?
body: Preload fetches critical resources, dns-prefetch resolves domain lookup only.

title: What is the difference between lazy loading images with loading="lazy" and JS-based lazy load?
body: Native loading="lazy" is browser-managed, JS-based uses IntersectionObserver.

title: What is the difference between srcdoc attribute in iframe and src?
body: srcdoc provides inline HTML code, src loads external URL.

title: What is the difference between <object> and <embed> tags?
body: <object> is more flexible and standard, <embed> is simpler but less supported.

title: What is the difference between inline-block and flex containers for HTML layouts?
body: Inline-block aligns inline but doesn’t support full layout features, flex provides alignment and spacing.

title: What is the difference between viewport units (vh, vw) and percentages?
body: VH/VW are relative to viewport size, % is relative to parent container.

title: What is the difference between nosniff header and MIME type in HTML resources?
body: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff prevents browser from guessing MIME type.

title: What is the difference between HTML parsing error handling in browsers?
body: Browsers follow error-tolerant parsing, not strict like XML.

title: What is the difference between <isindex> tag and modern search inputs?
body: <isindex> was an old single-input search element, replaced by <input type="search">.

title: What is the difference between Shadow DOM closed mode and open mode?
body: Open mode allows JS access via .shadowRoot, closed mode prevents it.

title: What is the difference between document.write and DOM methods for adding elements?
body: document.write blocks rendering and is discouraged, DOM methods are safer and dynamic.

title: Explain what CSS stands for.
body: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets, used to style HTML elements.

title: How do you link a CSS file to an HTML page?
body: Using the <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> tag inside <head>.

title: Which attribute inside HTML tags allows inline CSS?
body: The style attribute.

title: Give an example of a CSS property for text color.
body: color: red;

title: State the difference between inline, internal, and external CSS.
body: Inline uses style attribute, internal uses <style> inside HTML, external uses a separate .css file.

title: Mention the symbol used for IDs in CSS.
body: # is used for IDs.

title: Mention the symbol used for classes in CSS.
body: . is used for classes.

title: How do you change background color with CSS?
body: background-color: yellow;

title: Write the CSS to make text bold.
body: font-weight: bold;

title: Which CSS property is used for text size?
body: font-size

title: How do you underline text in CSS?
body: text-decoration: underline;

title: What is the default position property of HTML elements?
body: static

title: Name the CSS property used to align text to the center.
body: text-align: center;

title: How do you make a list without bullets using CSS?
body: list-style-type: none;

title: Which property controls spacing between lines of text?
body: line-height

title: How do you apply multiple classes to a single element?
body: Add them separated by spaces: class="class1 class2".

title: Which CSS property is used to add space inside an element’s border?
body: padding

title: Which CSS property adds space outside an element’s border?
body: margin

title: What is the difference between relative and absolute units in CSS?
body: Relative units depend on other values (e.g., %, em), absolute units are fixed (e.g., px).

title: How do you make an element’s font italic in CSS?
body: font-style: italic;

title: Which CSS property changes the typeface of text?
body: font-family

title: How do you change the width of a border in CSS?
body: Using border-width.

title: Write CSS to create a dashed border.
body: border: 2px dashed blue;

title: What is the difference between inline-block and block display?
body: Block takes full width, inline-block allows inline placement with block properties.

title: How do you hide an element but keep its space reserved?
body: visibility: hidden;

title: How do you hide an element and remove its space completely?
body: display: none;

title: Which property controls how content overflows a box?
body: overflow

title: Write CSS to make an element fixed at the top.
body: position: fixed; top: 0;

title: Explain the difference between absolute and fixed positioning.
body: Absolute is positioned relative to the nearest positioned ancestor, fixed is relative to the viewport.

title: Which CSS property controls cursor style?
body: cursor

title: How do you make a background image repeat horizontally only?
body: background-repeat: repeat-x;

title: Which property controls background image size?
body: background-size

title: How do you create a gradient background in CSS?
body: Using background: linear-gradient(color1, color2);

title: Which CSS property changes the opacity of an element?
body: opacity

title: What is the difference between em and rem units?
body: em is relative to parent font size, rem is relative to root font size.

title: Which property changes capitalization of text?
body: text-transform

title: Give the CSS to make the first letter of a paragraph larger.
body: Use pseudo-element: p::first-letter { font-size: 200%; }

How do you select all

tags inside a

?
body: div p { ... }

title: Which selector is used for hover effects?
body: :hover

title: Write CSS to apply style only to even rows of a table.
body: tr:nth-child(even) { ... }

title: How do you apply a style only if an input is focused?
body: Using input:focus { ... }

title: How do you center a block element horizontally with CSS?
body: margin: 0 auto;

title: Explain the difference between inline and block elements in CSS terms.
body: Inline doesn’t start on a new line, block takes full width.

title: Which CSS property controls element stacking order?
body: z-index

title: Which property allows rounded corners?
body: border-radius

title: What is the difference between relative and absolute paths in CSS URLs?
body: Relative depends on file location, absolute uses full path.

title: How do you make an image responsive in CSS?
body: max-width: 100%; height: auto;

title: Write CSS to fix a footer at the bottom of the page.
body: position: fixed; bottom: 0; width: 100%;

title: Which property is used for shadow effects?
body: box-shadow or text-shadow.

title: What is the difference between inline-style and external CSS in terms of performance?
body: External CSS is cached and reusable, inline must load every time.

title: Differentiate between relative, absolute, fixed, and sticky positioning.
body: Relative moves based on its normal position, absolute positions relative to ancestor, fixed is relative to viewport, sticky toggles between relative/fixed depending on scroll.

title: How does the z-index property work when elements overlap?
body: It defines stack order; higher values appear above lower ones, but only works on positioned elements.

title: Which CSS property ensures a child element doesn’t overflow its parent container?
body: overflow: hidden;

title: How would you make an element appear only on print view?
body: Use @media print { ... }.

title: What is the difference between inline-block and flex layout?
body: Inline-block arranges items inline but lacks advanced alignment; flex provides powerful alignment/distribution controls.

title: When should you use min-width vs max-width in media queries?
body: min-width applies styles on wider screens (mobile-first), max-width applies styles on narrower screens (desktop-first).

title: Explain the difference between absolute units (px) and relative units (em, %, vh).
body: Absolute is fixed; relative units scale based on parent or viewport.

title: How can you center an element vertically inside a container using Flexbox?
body: display: flex; align-items: center;

title: What is the difference between relative length units em and rem?
body: em depends on parent’s font size, rem depends on root (html) font size.

title: Which CSS property allows you to control the aspect ratio of elements?
body: aspect-ratio.

title: How do you select an element that comes immediately after another element?
body: Adjacent sibling selector A + B.

title: Explain the difference between pseudo-classes and pseudo-elements.
body: Pseudo-classes (:hover) define states, pseudo-elements (::before) create virtual elements.

title:
How would you apply a style to all

elements inside a

with class box?
body: .box p { ... }

title: Write CSS to make only the first child of a list bold.
body: li:first-child { font-weight: bold; }

title: What’s the difference between absolute and relative file paths in CSS url()?
body: Relative depends on stylesheet location, absolute includes full path.

title: How do you create a fixed responsive grid without using frameworks?
body: Use display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...));.

title: What is the difference between relative and sticky positioning?
body: Sticky behaves like relative until a scroll threshold, then sticks like fixed.

title: How do you apply different styles for dark mode users?
body: Using @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { ... }.

title: Write CSS to style all <input> elements except checkboxes.
body: input:not([type=checkbox]) { ... }

title: What is the difference between CSS transitions and animations?
body: Transitions need a trigger (like hover), animations run automatically with keyframes.

title: How can you create a triangle shape in CSS without images?
body: Using borders: width:0; height:0; border-left:...; border-right:...; border-bottom:...;.

title: Which CSS function is used for color transparency?
body: rgba() or hsla().

title: What is the difference between absolute and relative positioning inside a flex container?
body: Absolute ignores flex rules, relative still participates in flex layout.

title: How do you select every odd row of a table?
body: tr:nth-child(odd) { ... }

title: What does the clip-path property do?
body: Defines a visible region of an element, hiding the rest.

title: Explain the difference between inline SVG and CSS background SVG.
body: Inline SVG is part of DOM and styleable, background SVG is treated like an image.

title: How would you apply different styles for high-resolution screens (retina)?
body: Use @media only screen and (min-resolution: 2dppx) { ... }.

title: What is the difference between relative and absolute imports of fonts?
body: Relative depends on file location, absolute is a full URL (like Google Fonts).

title: How do CSS variables (--var) differ from preprocessor variables like SASS?
body: CSS variables are runtime and cascade; SASS variables are compile-time only.

title: Write CSS to apply hover effect only on devices that support hover.
body: @media (hover: hover) { a:hover { ... } }

title: How can you force an element to stay inside a parent even if larger?
body: overflow: auto; or max-width: 100%;.

title: What’s the difference between grid and flexbox?
body: Flexbox is one-dimensional (row or column), grid is two-dimensional (rows and columns).

title: How do you create equal column heights using flexbox?
body: Flex items automatically stretch by default (align-items: stretch).

title: Which property controls the order of flex items?
body: order property.

title: How do you center an absolutely positioned element both horizontally and vertically?
body: position: absolute; top:50%; left:50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);

title: What is the difference between relative and sticky positioning with scroll?
body: Sticky toggles between relative and fixed when reaching threshold, relative never fixes.

title: How do you select all elements with attribute starting with a certain value?
body: [attr^="value"]

title: Write CSS to add a custom cursor icon.
body: cursor: url('icon.png'), auto;

title: What’s the difference between inline style and CSS variables in <style>?
body: Inline style applies to single element, CSS variables can be reused globally.

title: Explain how the cascade works when multiple CSS rules apply.
body: CSS applies rules by specificity, importance (!important), and source order.

title: How do you apply style only to empty elements?
body: :empty pseudo-class.

title: What is the difference between visibility: hidden and opacity: 0?
body: visibility: hidden removes interaction, opacity: 0 keeps interaction.

title: Which CSS property defines flexible growth in flexbox?
body: flex-grow.

title: How do you prevent child elements from overflowing a flex container?
body: flex-wrap: wrap;.

title: Write CSS to select all links that open in a new tab.
body: a[target="_blank"] { ... }

title: How do you ensure a background image covers the full element?
body: background-size: cover;.

title: Which property helps in smooth scrolling to anchors?
body: scroll-behavior: smooth;.

title: Explain the difference between absolute and relative units in responsive design.
body: Absolute units don’t scale; relative units adjust with viewport or parent.

title: How do you force hardware acceleration for smoother animations?
body: Use transform: translateZ(0);.

title: What is the difference between inline-flex and flex?
body: inline-flex behaves like inline but children are flex items; flex is block-level.

title: How does the browser render CSS from parsing to painting?
body: It builds DOM + CSSOM, merges into render tree, computes layout, then paints pixels.

title: Explain reflow vs repaint in CSS.
body: Reflow recalculates positions/layout; repaint updates visuals without changing layout.

title: Which CSS properties trigger GPU acceleration?
body: Transforms (translate, scale, rotate) and opacity are GPU-accelerated.

title: Why can will-change improve performance but also harm it?
body: It hints the browser to optimize elements, but overuse consumes memory.

title: Differentiate between stacking context and z-index.
body: Stacking context is a hierarchy formed by certain properties; z-index works only within its context.

title: How do container queries differ from media queries?
body: Media queries depend on viewport size, container queries depend on parent container size.

title: What is the difference between CSS Grid subgrid and normal grid?
body: Subgrid allows child elements to inherit parent’s grid tracks for alignment.

title: Explain the concept of Critical CSS.
body: It’s the minimum CSS needed for above-the-fold content, loaded inline for faster rendering.

title: How do you implement CSS scoping without Shadow DOM?
body: Using :where(), BEM naming, or scoping classes.

title: Why is @layer introduced in CSS?
body: To control cascade layers explicitly and manage conflicts in large codebases.

title: How does CSS contain property improve performance?
body: It isolates rendering of elements to reduce reflow/repaint costs.

title: Explain the difference between subpixel rendering and normal rendering.
body: Subpixel rendering uses fractions of pixels to improve sharpness on high-DPI screens.

title: Why should you avoid * { margin:0; padding:0; } resets in large projects?
body: It can cause unnecessary reflows and override needed defaults; better to use modern normalize.css.

title: How do you optimize animations for performance?
body: Animate transform and opacity, avoid layout-affecting properties like width or top.

title: What is the difference between logical properties and physical properties in CSS?
body: Logical adapt to writing modes (margin-inline), physical are fixed (margin-left).

title: How do CSS custom properties differ from SASS variables at runtime?
body: CSS vars are live, cascade, and can change dynamically; SASS vars are compile-time only.

title: Why is position: sticky sometimes not working?
body: It needs a scrollable ancestor and a defined top/left/right/bottom offset.

title: How do you handle specificity wars in large projects?
body: Use cascade layers, utility classes, or naming conventions like BEM.

title: Explain difference between relative color syntax and traditional color functions.
body: Relative color syntax (e.g., color-mix()) allows manipulation based on existing colors.

title: How does clip-path: path() differ from SVG clipping?
body: clip-path applies CSS shapes, while SVG allows more complex paths and external references.

title: Why is CSS subgrid important for complex layouts?
body: It aligns nested elements with parent grid without duplicating track definitions.

title: What is the difference between :is() and :where()?
body: Both group selectors, but :where() has zero specificity, :is() takes the highest specificity.

title: How does prefers-reduced-motion improve accessibility?
body: It respects user OS settings and disables motion-heavy animations.

title: Write CSS to support both dark mode and high-contrast users.
body: Use combined media queries: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) and (prefers-contrast: more).

title: Why should inline critical CSS be minimized?
body: Too much inline CSS blocks rendering and prevents caching.

title: Explain difference between absolute and fixed background attachment.
body: Absolute scrolls with element, fixed stays relative to viewport.

title: What is the role of CSS Houdini?
body: It exposes low-level APIs to extend CSS, letting developers define custom styles.

title: How do you deploy a Next.js project to Vercel?
body: Push to GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket and connect to Vercel for automatic deployment.

title: How does Next.js support API versioning?
body: By creating versioned directories inside pages/api/, like api/v1 and api/v2.

title: How does static file caching work in Next.js?
body: Assets in public/ get cache-control headers for efficient caching.

title: How do you handle private environment variables in Next.js?
body: Store them in .env.local and never expose them to the client.

title: How do you use environment variables in client-side code safely?
body: Prefix them with NEXT_PUBLIC_.

title: Why might you use rewrites in Next.js?
body: To map incoming requests to different paths or external APIs without changing the URL.

title: How do you implement incremental static regeneration for a blog?
body: Use getStaticProps with a revalidate value and generate pages with getStaticPaths.

title: What’s the difference between pages/_app.js and pages/_document.js?
body: _app.js controls page initialization and global styles, _document.js customizes the HTML document structure.

title: How do you handle authentication in Next.js?
body: By using middleware, JWT tokens, or libraries like NextAuth.js.

title: How do you enable HTTPS locally with Next.js?
body: By using a custom server setup with Node.js/Express and SSL certificates.

title: Why should you use API routes instead of a separate backend?
body: For smaller apps, API routes simplify backend logic without extra servers.

title: How can you analyze bundle size in a Next.js project?
body: By using the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin.

title: What are dynamic imports and why are they useful in Next.js?
body: They allow lazy-loading components only when needed, improving performance.

title: How do you customize the default Babel or Webpack config in Next.js?
body: By modifying next.config.js with webpack or babel fields.

title: How can Next.js support both static and server-side rendering in one app?
body: By choosing getStaticProps for static pages and getServerSideProps for dynamic ones.

title: What happens if you don’t export a default component from a page file?
body: Next.js will throw an error, since every page must export a React component.

title: How do you create nested routes in Next.js?
body: By creating nested folders inside pages/.

title: What’s the difference between 404.js and _error.js?
body: 404.js handles “not found” pages, _error.js handles generic errors.

title: How can you serve a sitemap in Next.js?
body: Generate a sitemap XML file using an API route or static file under public/.

title: What is the difference between absolute imports and relative imports in Next.js?
body: Absolute imports simplify imports by using baseUrl in jsconfig.json or tsconfig.json.

title: How do you set up API rate limiting in Next.js?
body: By adding logic inside API routes or middleware to track requests per user/IP.

title: Can Next.js pages fetch GraphQL data?
body: Yes, using getServerSideProps or getStaticProps with a GraphQL client.

title: How does Next.js handle 500 errors by default?
body: It shows a generic error page unless you override with _error.js.

title: How do you enable image domains for next/image optimization?
body: Add allowed domains in images.domains inside next.config.js.

title: What is the difference between ISR and SSR with caching?
body: ISR updates static pages in the background, SSR regenerates fresh HTML on each request.

title: How can you integrate Redux with Next.js?
body: Wrap the app in a provider inside _app.js and configure the store with SSR support.

title: How would you debug a hydration mismatch error in Next.js?
body: Check for differences between server-rendered HTML and client-side render, ensure no browser-only APIs run during SSR, and use useEffect for client-only logic.

title: Describe a scenario where Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) could cause stale data. How do you solve it?
body: If a page is cached and revalidated after revalidate time, users may see old data. Use on-demand revalidation with res.revalidate() for instant refresh.

title: How do you secure API routes in Next.js from unauthorized access?
body: Use middleware for authentication, validate tokens (JWT, NextAuth), and restrict access in the API handler with role-based checks.

title: What’s the difference between using Next.js middleware and API routes for auth?
body: Middleware runs before a request reaches a page or API, good for redirects and access control; API routes handle data requests and business logic.

title: How would you implement server-side feature flags in Next.js?
body: Store feature flags in a config or remote service, check them in getServerSideProps or middleware, and conditionally render UI based on flags.

title: When should you prefer getInitialProps over getServerSideProps?
body: Rarely; getInitialProps works on both client and server but disables automatic static optimization. Used mostly in custom _app.js.

title: Explain how to handle large datasets in SSR pages without hitting performance issues.
body: Use pagination, streaming responses (Next.js 13 with React Server Components), or cache results via Edge Middleware/CDN.

title: How would you reduce bundle size in a Next.js project?
body: Dynamic imports, tree-shaking unused code, analyzing with next-bundle-analyzer, and splitting vendor libraries.

title: How do you integrate GraphQL efficiently with Next.js?
body: Use Apollo or URQL with SSR/SSG setup, prefetch queries in getServerSideProps or getStaticProps, and hydrate cache on the client.

title: How does Next.js handle route prefetching internally?
body: It preloads JavaScript and data for linked routes using next/link with prefetch={true}, caching them for instant navigation.

title: How can you debug slow page loads in production?
body: Use next build --profile, Lighthouse audits, bundle analyzer, check for blocking scripts, and measure server response times.

title: Describe a real-world scenario where Edge Functions in Next.js outperform SSR.
body: Personalization at the CDN edge, like geo-based redirects or A/B testing, without needing full SSR from origin.

title: How do you ensure sensitive environment variables aren’t leaked to the client?
body: Prefix only public variables with NEXT_PUBLIC_; keep private variables only in server code (API routes, getServerSideProps).

title: How do you implement custom caching headers in Next.js responses?
body: Modify headers in next.config.js with async headers(), or set in API routes using res.setHeader().

title: Explain the difference between ISR fallback modes: 'blocking', 'true', and 'false'.
body: false: only pre-rendered paths exist, 404 otherwise. true: serve fallback page, then update. blocking: wait for server to generate before serving.

title: How would you implement multi-tenant applications in Next.js?
body: Use dynamic routing with subdomains or path prefixes, middleware for tenant detection, and tenant-specific config.

title: What is streaming in React Server Components, and how does Next.js use it?
body: Streaming allows partial page rendering while fetching other data, improving performance. Next.js 13+ supports it with Suspense.

title: How do you optimize API calls in a Next.js SSR page that fetches multiple data sources?
body: Use Promise.all, cache results, or parallelize requests to reduce blocking time.

title: Describe how to migrate a Next.js app from Pages Router to App Router.
body: Convert _app.js/_document.js logic to layouts, move getServerSideProps to fetch inside Server Components, use route.ts for APIs.

title: How can you handle authentication with SSR in Next.js App Router?
body: Use getServerSession from NextAuth, fetch user session inside server components, and conditionally render protected UI.

title: Why might an API route inside Next.js scale poorly, and how do you fix it?
body: Because Next.js API routes run on Node server; for scale, offload to serverless (Vercel Functions) or external APIs.

title: How do you track memory leaks in a Next.js app?
body: Use Node.js heap snapshots, check long-running SSR functions, and monitor for event listeners not removed.

title: Explain a case where dynamic imports could break SSR.
body: If a dynamically imported component depends on window or client APIs, SSR will fail; must use ssr: false.

title: How do you optimize SEO for dynamic routes in Next.js?
body: Use getStaticPaths with getStaticProps for pre-rendering, add meta tags in <Head>, and generate dynamic sitemaps.

title: How would you implement custom 404 and 500 pages?
body: Create pages/404.js and pages/500.js, or with App Router, define not-found.js and error.js.

title: How does Next.js handle internationalization internally?
body: It rewrites routes with locale prefixes, uses routing context to resolve translations, and supports domain-based locales.

title: How do you handle rate-limiting in Next.js API routes?
body: Use Redis or in-memory counters with middleware, block requests exceeding thresholds, or use edge functions for distributed limits.

title: How would you implement real-time features like chat in Next.js?
body: Use WebSockets (Socket.io), Pusher, or SSE inside API routes or serverless functions.

title: How can you detect and fix layout shift issues (CLS) in Next.js apps?
body: Predefine image dimensions, use next/image with fill or width/height, and minimize dynamic content injection.

title: How do you deploy a hybrid Next.js app (SSG + SSR + ISR) on AWS?
body: Use AWS Lambda for SSR/ISR, S3 + CloudFront for static assets, and DynamoDB/Redis for caching.

title: How can you enforce strict CSP headers in Next.js?
body: Add headers in next.config.js or middleware, define CSP rules, and ensure nonce for inline scripts.

title: How do you implement role-based routing in Next.js App Router?
body: Use middleware to check user roles, redirect unauthorized users, and secure server components conditionally.

title: How would you implement a headless CMS with Next.js ISR?
body: Fetch CMS content in getStaticProps, enable revalidation, and trigger on-demand revalidation when content changes.

title: How do you test API routes in Next.js?
body: Use Jest + Supertest, mock req/res objects, and verify response codes and payloads.

title: How can you debug Next.js middleware issues in production?
body: Add logging, test locally with next dev, and simulate edge environments with Vercel CLI.

title: How do you scale Next.js on Docker + Kubernetes?
body: Use multi-stage Docker builds, serve static files via CDN, autoscale SSR pods, and manage sticky sessions if needed.

title: Explain how Next.js supports React 18 concurrent features.
body: It uses React Server Components, Suspense for data fetching, and streaming SSR for faster page rendering.

title: How can you pre-render private pages but still enforce auth?
body: Use SSR with session check in getServerSideProps, render skeleton UI, then redirect if unauthorized.

title: What’s the impact of turning off static optimization in Next.js?
body: All pages become server-rendered, increasing load time and server costs.

title: How do you optimize large forms in Next.js with SSR validation?
body: Use React Hook Form, debounce inputs, validate server-side in API routes, and preload error messages.

title: How do you handle breaking API changes in a Next.js monorepo?
body: Version APIs (v1, v2 folders), deprecate old routes gradually, and manage builds with Turborepo.

title: How can you achieve zero-downtime deployments in Next.js?
body: Use blue-green or canary deployments with Vercel or Kubernetes, cache busting for assets, and ISR fallback.

title: Why might you use Edge Middleware instead of rewriting routes in Next.js?
body: Middleware executes before request routing, allowing faster redirects, auth checks, or geolocation logic.

title: How do you ensure images in Next.js don’t break in production?
body: Configure domains in next.config.js, use next/image loader properly, and optimize caching/CDN.

title: How would you debug a failing dynamic route deployment?
body: Check getStaticPaths return values, ensure fallback is configured, and test route parameters locally.

title: How do you secure sensitive pages in static builds (SSG)?
body: You can’t directly; protect with middleware, serverless API auth, or move to SSR for secure pages.

title: How do you use revalidation in the App Router compared to Pages Router?
body: App Router uses fetch with { next: { revalidate: N } }, while Pages Router uses revalidate in getStaticProps.

title: What’s the difference between rewriting and redirecting in Next.js?
body: Redirect changes URL in browser (SEO impact), rewrite keeps URL same but serves another route.

title: How would you track and fix memory bloat in Next.js ISR?
body: Monitor cache size, purge old builds, and use on-demand revalidation instead of frequent static regenerations.

title: How do you implement micro-frontends with Next.js?
body: Use Module Federation, separate Next.js apps per domain, integrate via reverse proxy or middleware.

title: What is Remix used for?
body: Remix is a full-stack web framework for building React apps with server-side rendering and routing.

title: Who created Remix?
body: Remix was created by the React Router team (Michael Jackson and Ryan Florence).

title: Is Remix built on React?
body: Yes, Remix is a framework on top of React.

title: How is Remix different from Next.js?
body: Remix focuses on web standards, nested routing, and built-in data loading, while Next.js emphasizes static generation and hybrid rendering.

title: Can Remix run on Node.js?
body: Yes, Remix apps run on Node.js environments like Express.

title: What is the default file extension for Remix routes?
body: .tsx or .jsx files inside the app/routes/ folder.

title: What is the folder where Remix routes live?
body: The app/routes/ folder.

title: Which file runs first in a Remix app?
body: root.tsx (or root.jsx) is the entry point.

title: How do you start a new Remix project?
body: By running npx create-remix@latest.

title: Which command runs Remix in development mode?
body: npm run dev or yarn dev.

title: How do you define a route in Remix?
body: By creating a file inside the app/routes/ directory, like about.tsx.

title: What is Remix’s default styling option?
body: Plain CSS is supported out of the box.

title: Can Remix use Tailwind CSS?
body: Yes, Tailwind CSS can be integrated easily in Remix.

title: Which package is required for routing in Remix?
body: react-router (Remix is built on React Router).

title: Does Remix support nested routes?
body: Yes, Remix has built-in nested routing.

title: What does <Outlet /> do in Remix?
body: It renders child routes inside a parent route.

title: How do you create a layout in Remix?
body: By using nested routes and <Outlet /> for child content.

title: What is a loader in Remix?
body: A server-side function that fetches data before rendering a route.

title: How do you export a loader in Remix?
body: By writing export const loader = async () => { ... }.

title: What hook is used to access loader data?
body: useLoaderData().

title: Can Remix fetch data on the client side?
body: Yes, using fetch or React query libraries.

title: What is an action in Remix?
body: A server-side function that handles form submissions and mutations.

title: How do you export an action in Remix?
body: By writing export const action = async () => { ... }.

title: Which hook is used to handle form state in Remix?
body: useActionData().

title: What component is used for forms in Remix?
body: <Form> component.

title: Does Remix require client-side JavaScript for forms?
body: No, forms work with server actions without client JS.

title: How do you do redirects in Remix?
body: By returning redirect('/path') from loader or action.

title: What is meta function used for in Remix?
body: To define page metadata like title and description.

title: How do you export a meta function in Remix?
body: export const meta = () => [{ title: "My Page" }].

title: How can you link to another route in Remix?
body: By using <Link to="/about">.

title: Which hook is used for navigation in Remix?
body: useNavigate().

title: What does useFetcher() do in Remix?
body: It lets you fetch data or submit forms without navigation.

title: How do you show errors in Remix routes?
body: By using an ErrorBoundary component.

title: Which hook provides the current route params?
body: useParams().

title: Can Remix work with TypeScript?
body: Yes, Remix has full TypeScript support.

title: What command builds a Remix app for production?
body: npm run build.

title: How do you deploy a Remix app to Vercel?
body: Use the Vercel Remix adapter and run vercel deploy.

title: Can Remix be deployed on Netlify?
body: Yes, with the Netlify Remix adapter.

title: What is Remix Stacks?
body: Pre-configured templates with Remix + database + auth + deployment setup.

title: What database ORM works well with Remix?
body: Prisma is commonly used with Remix.

title: What is the purpose of remix.config.js?
body: It configures the Remix app (routes, server, build).

title: How do you add global styles in Remix?
body: By exporting links() in root.tsx with stylesheet references.

title: Does Remix support environment variables?
body: Yes, they can be accessed via process.env.

title: How can you serve static files in Remix?
body: Place them in the public/ directory.

title: What is a resource route in Remix?
body: A route that only returns data (like JSON or API).

title: How do you create a resource route in Remix?
body: By exporting a loader or action without a component.

title: Can Remix render on the server?
body: Yes, Remix apps support full SSR.

title: Can Remix generate static pages?
body: Yes, though its main focus is SSR.

title: How do you handle 404 pages in Remix?
body: By creating a CatchBoundary in routes.

title: What hook returns transition states for navigation?
body: useTransition().

title: How is data loading in Remix different from traditional React apps?
body: Remix fetches data on the server with loader before rendering, unlike React which fetches on the client after mount.

title: Why does Remix prefer web standards for forms instead of custom JavaScript?
body: Because native <form> elements work with HTTP requests, progressive enhancement, and degrade gracefully without JS.

title: In which case would you use useFetcher() instead of <Form>?
body: When you need to submit data or load data without causing a route navigation.

title: What happens if both a loader and an action are defined in a route?
body: Loader runs for GET requests; Action runs for POST/PUT/DELETE requests.

title: How would you prefetch data in Remix routes?
body: Use <Link prefetch="intent"> to load data early when a user is likely to navigate.

title: Why is nested routing powerful in Remix?
body: It allows each route to have its own data loader and UI, composing layouts naturally.

title: How can you pass data from a parent route loader to child routes?
body: Parent loader returns data; children can access it using useMatches().

title: What is the difference between useLoaderData() and useMatches()?
body: useLoaderData() gives current route data; useMatches() can access data from all matched routes.

title: How does Remix handle errors differently from React?
body: Remix uses ErrorBoundary and CatchBoundary at route level for precise error handling.

title: How can you handle 404 errors in Remix?
body: By throwing a Response with status 404 in a loader, then handling it in a CatchBoundary.

title: When would you use resource routes in Remix?
body: When you need an API endpoint returning JSON, XML, or other non-HTML responses.

title: How do you return JSON from a loader?
body: Use return json({ key: value }) from @remix-run/node.

title: What’s the difference between redirect() and json() in Remix loaders?
body: redirect() sends a 302 redirect; json() sends structured JSON data.

title: How do you handle authentication in Remix loaders?
body: Check cookies/sessions in the loader, redirect unauthenticated users, or return user data for rendering.

title: What’s the difference between using sessions and JWTs in Remix apps?
body: Sessions store state on the server (cookie-based), JWTs are stateless and stored client-side.

title: Why is it important that loaders run on the server?
body: It improves performance, SEO, and keeps sensitive API keys safe from the client.

title: How would you share global data like user info across routes?
body: Fetch it in root.tsx loader and access with useLoaderData() or useMatches().

title: Can actions return values other than redirects?
body: Yes, actions can return JSON, form errors, or custom responses.

title: How can you handle form validation in Remix actions?
body: Validate server-side inside the action and return errors using useActionData().

title: How do you prevent duplicate form submissions in Remix?
body: Use useTransition() to disable the submit button while the request is processing.

title: How does Remix optimize for fast page navigation?
body: By prefetching data, using nested routes, and avoiding client-side waterfalls.

title: What does the defer() function do in Remix?
body: It allows streaming responses by deferring part of the loader data until it’s ready.

title: When should you use defer()?
body: For large or slow-loading data that doesn’t block initial page render.

title: How would you integrate a database like Prisma in Remix loaders?
body: Call Prisma queries directly inside loaders/actions (on the server) and return results.

title: Why is Remix good for SEO?
body: It renders on the server with fresh data and exposes full HTML to search engines.

title: How can you add meta tags dynamically in Remix?
body: Export a meta function in route files and return title/description from loader data.

title: How does Remix handle styles differently than CRA?
body: Remix loads CSS via links in links() export, not via JS-injected styles.

title: How do you add a page-specific stylesheet in Remix?
body: Export links() in a route component to attach a stylesheet.

title: How would you load fonts in Remix?
body: Use <link> in links() or place font files in the public/ directory.

title: Why is Remix better for progressive enhancement than SPA frameworks?
body: Because Remix apps still work without JavaScript due to server-side rendering and HTML-first approach.

title: How do you fetch environment variables in Remix safely?
body: Use server-side loaders to access process.env, avoid exposing them directly to the client.

title: How does Remix compare with Express for building web apps?
body: Remix is higher-level, providing routing, SSR, and data loading out of the box; Express is lower-level middleware.

title: When would you choose resource routes over API routes in another backend?
body: When you want Remix itself to serve the data instead of calling an external API.

title: How does Remix help with accessibility?
body: Nested routing ensures consistent layouts, <Form> uses semantic HTML, and built-in error handling supports ARIA.

title: How do you handle file uploads in Remix?
body: Use a <Form encType="multipart/form-data"> and process in the action using Node’s APIs or a library.

title: How do you set cookies in Remix?
body: Use createCookie or createSessionStorage from @remix-run/node.

title: How do you secure cookies in Remix?
body: Use httpOnly, secure, and sameSite options when creating the cookie.

title: How can you stream data in Remix?
body: Use defer() with React Suspense to stream parts of loader data.

title: What is Remix’s approach to client-side caching?
body: Remix relies on HTTP caching headers rather than in-app JS caching.

title: How would you handle API errors in Remix?
body: Throw a Response with appropriate status codes and catch it in a CatchBoundary.

title: What is the difference between CatchBoundary and ErrorBoundary?
body: CatchBoundary handles thrown Responses (like 404); ErrorBoundary handles runtime errors.

title: How do you conditionally show navigation links in Remix based on login?
body: Check session in loader, return user object, and render nav links accordingly.

title: How can you handle background tasks in Remix?
body: Trigger async work in an action and return immediately, or use a job queue on the server.

title: What happens if you call useLoaderData() in a component without a loader?
body: It will throw an error, since no data is provided for that route.

title: Why does Remix encourage colocation of routes and data loaders?
body: It keeps UI and data logic together, making code easier to maintain.

title: How can Remix apps be deployed on serverless platforms?
body: Using official adapters li

title: How do you test Remix loaders and actions?
body: Unit-test loaders/actions by calling them directly with mocked Request/params and checking the returned Response/data; for full behavior use integration or E2E tests (Jest + Supertest, Playwright/Cypress) to exercise real requests and form submissions.

title: How do you protect Remix forms from CSRF attacks?
body: Issue a server-side CSRF token (or use a SameSite, HttpOnly session cookie) and include/validate the token in the form action; also validate Origin/Referer headers and use secure cookies to reduce CSRF risk.

title: How can you implement optimistic UI updates for form submissions in Remix?
body: Update UI immediately on submit (local state or useFetcher()), send the action request, then reconcile the server response — show success or rollback state on error; use useTransition() to show pending status.

title: How do you implement localization (i18n) in a Remix app using loaders?
body: Detect the locale in the loader (from Accept-Language, a cookie, or route param), load the appropriate translation/resources on the server (e.g., JSON files or a translations service), return them via useLoaderData() and render server-side for SEO. Persist the user choice in a cookie or locale-prefixed routes (/en/*, /fr/*). Common libraries like i18next or FormatJS can be used, but keep fetching/selection logic inside loaders so content is SSR-friendly.

title: How would you scale a large Remix app with micro-frontends?
body: Split features into independent Remix apps or routes, deploy separately, and integrate via reverse proxy or module federation. Each micro-app can share auth and design system while scaling independently.

title: How can you optimize Remix for extremely high-traffic SSR workloads?
body: Use streaming responses, CDN edge caching, serverless deployment (e.g., Vercel/Netlify), database connection pooling, and load balancing with sticky sessions if needed.

title: Explain how Remix handles concurrent requests differently than traditional Express apps.
body: Remix treats each request as isolated, leveraging serverless or per-request context, avoiding shared global state, whereas Express apps often maintain long-lived processes with potential race conditions.

title: How do you integrate Remix with GraphQL subscriptions for real-time updates?
body: Set up a GraphQL server (Apollo/Helix) with WebSockets, then consume data in Remix loaders/actions or directly in components via Apollo client; fallback to SSE where WebSockets aren’t possible.

title: What’s the approach to implement custom caching strategies in Remix?
body: Use HTTP headers (Cache-Control, ETag), conditional requests in loaders, server-side in-memory caching (e.g., Redis), and Remix’s headers() function to propagate cache hints.

title: How do you ensure Remix apps remain resilient during partial backend outages?
body: Implement graceful fallbacks in loaders (return default data, cached data, or error boundaries), circuit breakers for failing APIs, and service mesh retries (e.g., Istio).

title: How would you secure Remix apps deployed on multiple environments (edge, server, hybrid)?
body: Use environment-specific secrets management (Vault, AWS SSM), enforce HTTPS everywhere, consistent CSP headers, and align cookie settings (Secure, SameSite, HttpOnly) across all deployments.

title: How do you integrate Remix with a headless CMS at scale?
body: Fetch data in loaders from CMS APIs (Contentful, Sanity, Strapi), implement caching and revalidation strategies, and use incremental static regeneration-like approaches with webhooks for cache busting.

title: How would you handle SEO challenges with multilingual Remix apps?
body: Use locale-specific routes, <link rel="alternate" hreflang> tags, server-rendered meta data, canonical tags, and sitemap generation per locale.

title: Can Remix work with WebAssembly (Wasm)? How?
body: Yes — load Wasm modules in loaders (for server-side computation) or in the browser with WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(), then hydrate results into components.

title: How can you handle file uploads >100MB in Remix?
body: Stream uploads directly to object storage (S3, GCP) using signed URLs, avoid buffering in memory, and process metadata in Remix actions.

title: How does Remix’s request lifecycle differ when deployed to serverless vs traditional servers?
body: On serverless, each request has cold-start latency and no shared state; Remix still runs loaders/actions per request. On long-lived servers, global state may persist but must be managed carefully.

title: How would you implement zero-downtime deployment for a Remix app?
body: Use blue-green or rolling deployments, database migrations with backward compatibility, and sticky sessions (if session-based auth) during rollout.

title: What is the role of streaming in Remix SSR, and how does it compare to React 18 Suspense streaming?
body: Remix streams HTML progressively using node streams or web streams, enabling faster TTFB. Combined with React 18 Suspense, partial UI can stream while data is loading.

title: How do you prevent N+1 database query issues in Remix loaders?
body: Use batching (DataLoader), joins, or query optimization in ORMs. Since loaders run server-side, database optimizations are critical.

title: How do you integrate Remix with WebSockets or Socket.IO?
body: Establish a WebSocket server (or Socket.IO) alongside Remix, then consume events client-side. Server-sent events can also integrate directly into loaders.

title: Explain how Remix handles CSP (Content Security Policy).
body: Remix provides meta handling in routes; developers must define Content-Security-Policy headers in loaders or via server config. Nonces or hashes are needed for inline scripts.

title: How do you design a Remix app to support offline-first PWA capabilities?
body: Use service workers (Workbox), cache Remix routes with Cache API, pre-cache critical assets, and fallback loaders to cached data when offline.

title: What is the best way to implement feature flags in Remix?
body: Load flags from config or remote service in loaders, expose via useLoaderData, and use conditional rendering in routes. For SSR, flags must be server-evaluated.

title: How would you implement role-based access control in Remix routes?
