title: What is the difference between ng-if and ng-show?
body: ng-if removes/adds elements from the DOM, while ng-show only hides/shows elements with CSS.

title: What is AngularJS bootstrap process?
body: The process of starting an AngularJS app by loading the module, compiling the DOM, and linking the scope.

title: Can AngularJS apps run without ng-app?
body: No, without ng-app, AngularJS will not know where to start the application.

title: What is form validation in AngularJS?
body: AngularJS provides validation directives like ng-required, ng-minlength, ng-pattern for validating forms.

title: What is $valid in AngularJS forms?
body: A property that indicates if a form input is valid.

title: What is $dirty in AngularJS forms?
body: A property that indicates if a form input has been modified.

title: How is AngularJS different from jQuery?
body: AngularJS is a full MVC framework for building SPAs, while jQuery is a library for DOM manipulation and events.

title: Why do we use $scope instead of plain JavaScript variables?
body: $scope keeps data and view in sync via two-way binding, while normal variables won’t update the UI automatically.

title: In which cases would you use $rootScope?
body: For sharing data across multiple controllers. Example: user session details.

title: How do controllers communicate with each other?
body: Using $rootScope, services, or events ($emit, $broadcast, $on).

title: What is the difference between $emit and $broadcast?
body: $emit sends an event upwards, $broadcast sends it downwards in the scope hierarchy.

title: How do you make an AngularJS app modular?
body: By splitting features into multiple modules and injecting them as dependencies.

title: Why do we use dependency injection in AngularJS?
body: To make components reusable, testable, and loosely coupled.

title: What are custom services?
body: Developer-defined services created using .service() or .factory() for reusable logic.

title: Difference between .service() and .factory()?
body: .service() instantiates an object with new, .factory() returns the object directly.

title: What are constants in AngularJS?
body: Fixed values registered with .constant() that are available during app configuration and runtime.

title: When should you use .value() vs .constant()?
body: Use .value() for runtime-only values; .constant() for values needed during config phase.

title: What is $provide service?
body: A low-level API to register services, factories, values, and constants.

title: Why do we use $compile service?
body: To manually compile HTML strings or DOM into AngularJS templates.

title: What is $parse in AngularJS?
body: A service that converts AngularJS expressions into functions.

title: What does the $interpolate service do?
body: It compiles template strings with embedded expressions (like {{ }}) into a function.

title: How do you optimize digest cycles in AngularJS?
body: By minimizing watchers, using one-time binding (::), and avoiding deep $watch.

title: What is one-time binding in AngularJS?
body: Syntax {{ ::expression }} binds the value only once, not watching for future changes.

title: What are AngularJS decorators?
body: Functions used to modify or extend services before they are used.

title: How is $digest different from $apply?
body: $digest runs on current scope only, $apply triggers digest on all scopes.

title: What are isolate scopes in AngularJS directives?
body: A way to create a directive with its own private scope, preventing conflicts.

title: How do you pass data into directives?
body: Using @ (string), = (two-way binding), and & (function binding) in directive scope definition.

title: What are directive controllers?
body: They provide APIs for communication between directives.

title: What are transclusion directives?
body: Directives that capture and include the original content inside the directive’s template.

title: Give an example of built-in transclusion directive.
body: <ng-transclude> inside a custom directive.

title: What is the difference between compile and link functions in a directive?
body: Compile manipulates template DOM before it’s linked, Link binds scope to the DOM.

title: What is a pre-link and post-link function?
body: Pre-link runs before child elements are linked, post-link runs after.

title: What are filters chaining in AngularJS?
body: Applying multiple filters in sequence, e.g. `{{ name

title: How can you create a custom filter?
body: Using app.filter('filterName', function(){ return function(input){...}; });.

title: What is $filter service?
body: A service that allows programmatic use of filters inside controllers or services.

title: What are interceptors in AngularJS $http?
body: Functions that intercept requests or responses for logging, headers, or error handling.

title: How do you configure an $http interceptor?
body: By pushing it into $httpProvider.interceptors array during config.

title: How is AngularJS routing different from server-side routing?
body: AngularJS routing changes views without full page reload, server-side reloads the page.

title: What are route resolvers?
body: A way to fetch data before a route loads using resolve property in $routeProvider.

title: What is ui-router?
body: A popular third-party AngularJS routing library that supports nested states.

title: Difference between ngRoute and ui-router?
body: ngRoute is simple and route-based, ui-router is state-based with advanced nesting.

title: How does AngularJS handle asynchronous operations?
body: Using promises via $q service or $http service.

title: What is $q service in AngularJS?
body: A service for creating and managing promises.

title: How do you create a promise with $q?
body: Using $q.defer() which returns a deferred object with resolve and reject.

title: What are animations in AngularJS?
body: Visual effects added to DOM changes using ngAnimate module and CSS/JS hooks.

title: How do you include ngAnimate in an app?
body: By adding ngAnimate module as a dependency: angular.module('app',['ngAnimate']);.

title: Give an example of AngularJS animation class.
body: .ng-enter, .ng-leave, .ng-move for DOM transitions.

title: What are $resource services?
body: A higher-level abstraction over $http for working with RESTful APIs.

title: How do you define a $resource?
body: Using app.factory('MyResource', function($resource){ return $resource('/api/:id'); });.

title: What is the difference between $http and $resource?
body: $http is low-level for AJAX calls, $resource is higher-level for RESTful APIs.

title: What are form states in AngularJS?
body: $pristine, $dirty, $touched, $untouched, $valid, $invalid.

title: How do you disable a submit button until form is valid?
body: <button ng-disabled="formName.$invalid">Submit</button>.

title: What is $error object in AngularJS forms?
body: It stores validation errors for each form control.

title: How can AngularJS work with REST APIs?
body: Using $http, $resource, or third-party libraries like Restangular.

title: What is $cacheFactory in AngularJS?
body: A service for creating caches to store reusable data in memory.

title: When should you use $timeout over $interval?
body: $timeout is for delayed single execution, $interval for repeated execution.

title: How does AngularJS handle dirty checking internally?
body: It uses the digest cycle to repeatedly check watched variables and update the DOM when changes are detected.

title: Why is AngularJS considered slow with many watchers?
body: Because each digest cycle checks all watchers; a large number of watchers increases processing time.

title: How can you reduce the number of watchers in an AngularJS app?
body: Use one-time bindings (::), avoid deep $watch, and use track by in ng-repeat.

title: What is the role of $evalAsync in AngularJS?
body: It schedules an expression to be executed later in the current digest cycle.

title: Difference between $evalAsync and $timeout(fn,0)?
body: $evalAsync executes within the same digest, $timeout schedules for the next tick.

title: How do you manually trigger change detection in AngularJS?
body: By calling $scope.$apply() or $scope.$digest().

title: Why can $apply() cause performance issues?
body: It runs a full digest cycle on all scopes, which can be expensive in large apps.

title: How do you safely update scope outside AngularJS context (e.g., from a third-party library)?
body: Wrap the update in $scope.$apply() so AngularJS detects the change.

title: What is a memory leak in AngularJS apps?
body: When scopes, watchers, or DOM nodes are not properly destroyed, consuming memory unnecessarily.

title: How can you avoid memory leaks in AngularJS?
body: Deregister watchers, destroy scopes on route change, and unbind event listeners.

title: How do you debug performance bottlenecks in AngularJS?
body: By profiling watchers with tools like Batarang or custom $watch counters.

title: What is $destroy in AngularJS?
body: An event triggered when a scope is removed, used for cleanup.

title: How do you remove a watcher in AngularJS?
body: $watch returns a deregistration function that can be called to remove it.

title: What is the role of $exceptionHandler?
body: It handles uncaught exceptions in AngularJS and can be customized for logging.

title: How would you handle global error logging in AngularJS?
body: By decorating $exceptionHandler and sending logs to a server.

title: How do you customize AngularJS services with $provide.decorator?
body: It allows modifying or extending existing services before they are used.

title: What is the difference between $broadcast, $emit, and $on?
body: $broadcast sends events downward, $emit upward, $on listens for events.

title: Why should event-based communication be minimized in AngularJS?
body: It creates tight coupling and makes debugging harder.

title: How do you test AngularJS controllers?
body: By injecting $controller service in unit tests and mocking dependencies.

title: How do you test AngularJS directives?
body: By compiling the directive with $compile and inspecting the resulting DOM.

title: How do you mock HTTP requests in AngularJS tests?
body: Using $httpBackend service to define fake responses.

title: How do you ensure unit tests do not leak $httpBackend calls?
body: Always call $httpBackend.verifyNoOutstandingExpectation() and $httpBackend.verifyNoOutstandingRequest().

title: What is Protractor in AngularJS testing?
body: An end-to-end testing framework built on WebDriverJS for Angular apps.

title: How do you synchronize Protractor with AngularJS?
body: Protractor automatically waits for AngularJS to finish its digest cycles and async tasks.

title: How do you optimize AngularJS app startup time?
body: Lazy load modules, minimize watchers, and use async script loading.

title: What is lazy loading in AngularJS?
body: Loading modules, controllers, or components only when required.

title: How do you implement lazy loading in AngularJS?
body: With third-party libraries like ocLazyLoad.

title: What are the limitations of AngularJS digest cycle?
body: It only checks for reference changes, not deep object changes unless specified.

title: How do you watch a deep object in AngularJS?
body: Use $scope.$watch('obj', callback, true).

title: Why is deep watching discouraged?
body: It is expensive as AngularJS checks every property recursively.

title: How do you handle large lists efficiently in AngularJS?
body: Use track by in ng-repeat, pagination, and virtualization.

title: What is track by in ng-repeat?
body: A way to uniquely identify items in a collection to reduce DOM re-rendering.

title: How can you debug AngularJS digest cycle issues?
body: Use $watch logging, Batarang, or add console traces in $digest.

title: How does AngularJS handle security?
body: It sanitizes expressions and provides $sce for handling trusted content.

title: What is $sce in AngularJS?
body: Strict Contextual Escaping service for safely binding HTML, URLs, and resources.

title: How do you bypass sanitization in AngularJS?
body: By using $sce.trustAsHtml() or similar methods, but with caution.

title: What are AngularJS interceptors used for in production apps?
body: For adding auth tokens, logging requests, or handling global errors.

title: How do you implement authentication in AngularJS?
body: By using route guards, $http interceptors, and token-based login.

title: What is a digest cycle overflow error?
body: When $digest is called recursively more than 10 times, AngularJS throws an error.

title: What causes digest overflow errors?
body: Circular updates in watchers or incorrect $apply() usage.

title: How do you prevent digest overflow?
body: Avoid recursive scope updates and validate watcher logic.

title: What are some limitations of AngularJS compared to modern frameworks?
body: Performance with large apps, limited mobile support, and no built-in component system.

title: How do you migrate from AngularJS to Angular?
body: Use ngUpgrade to run both frameworks side by side and migrate gradually.

title: What is ngUpgrade?
body: A library to allow Angular and AngularJS code to coexist during migration.

title: How do you share services between AngularJS and Angular during migration?
body: By upgrading AngularJS services or downgrading Angular services.

title: How do you migrate routing from AngularJS to Angular?
body: Use Angular’s Router after downgrading components or use hybrid routes.

title: What are common anti-patterns in AngularJS apps?
body: Too many watchers, using $rootScope excessively, deep $watch, and large controllers.

title: How do you handle SEO in AngularJS apps?
body: Use server-side pre-rendering or tools like Prerender.io since AngularJS is client-rendered.

title: How do you internationalize AngularJS apps?
body: Using libraries like angular-translate and loading language files dynamically.

title: Why is AngularJS considered legacy today?
body: Because it has been deprecated and replaced by modern Angular (2+).

title: What is Vue.js?
body: A progressive JavaScript framework for building user interfaces and single-page applications.

title: Who created Vue.js?
body: Evan You created Vue.js in 2014.

title: Is Vue.js an open-source framework?
body: Yes, it is completely open-source.

title: What is the current stable version of Vue.js?
body: Vue 3.x is the current stable version.

title: What does “progressive framework” mean in Vue.js?
body: You can adopt Vue.js gradually, starting small and scaling up as needed.

title: What type of architecture does Vue.js use?
body: Component-based architecture.

title: What is a Vue instance?
body: The root object created with new Vue() that controls the Vue app.

title: What is the root element of a Vue app?
body: Usually an element with id="app" where Vue mounts.

title: How do you create a Vue instance?
body: new Vue({ el: '#app', data: { message: 'Hello' } });.

title: What is the el option in Vue?
body: It tells Vue which DOM element to mount the app on.

title: What is the data option in Vue?
body: An object that holds reactive properties for the Vue instance.

title: What is string interpolation in Vue.js?
body: Using double curly braces {{ }} to display data in templates.

title: What is a Vue directive?
body: A special token in markup like v-bind, v-if, v-for, which extends HTML.

title: What does v-bind do?
body: Dynamically binds HTML attributes to Vue data.

title: What does v-model do?
body: Creates two-way data binding between form inputs and Vue data.

title: What does v-if do?
body: Conditionally renders elements based on a boolean expression.

title: What is the difference between v-if and v-show?
body: v-if adds/removes elements from DOM, v-show only toggles CSS display.

title: What does v-for do?
body: Loops over an array or object to render elements.

title: How do you bind a CSS class in Vue.js?
body: Using v-bind:class or shorthand :class.

title: How do you bind inline styles in Vue.js?
body: Using v-bind:style or shorthand :style.

title: What is the Vue template syntax?
body: HTML-based syntax that allows using Vue’s directives and interpolation.

title: What is a Vue component?
body: A reusable and self-contained block of UI in Vue.js.

title: How do you register a global component?
body:
Vue.component('my-component', { template: '
...
' });.

title: How do you register a local component?
body: Inside the components option of a Vue instance or component.

title: What are props in Vue.js?
body: Custom attributes used to pass data from parent to child components.

title: What is the difference between props and data in Vue?
body: Props are external, passed by parent; data is internal, owned by the component.

title: How do you emit an event from a child component?
body: Using $emit('eventName', data).

title: How does a parent listen to a child event?
body: With v-on:eventName="handler" or @eventName="handler".

title: What is computed in Vue.js?
body: Properties that are cached and only re-evaluated when dependencies change.

title: How is computed different from methods?
body: Computed properties are cached, methods run every time they’re called.

title: What is a watcher in Vue.js?
body: A function that watches a reactive property and runs when it changes.

title: What is v-on used for?
body: Attaching event listeners to DOM elements.

title: What is the shorthand for v-on?
body: The @ symbol. Example: @click="handler".

title: What is the shorthand for v-bind?
body: The : symbol. Example: :src="image".

title: What is Vue Router?
body: The official routing library for Vue.js applications.

title: What is Vuex?
body: A state management library for Vue.js.

title: Is Vuex required for every Vue project?
body: No, it’s optional; mainly used for complex state management.

title: What is the difference between Vue.js and React?
body: Vue uses templates, React uses JSX. Vue has reactivity built-in, React uses virtual DOM diffing.

title: What is the difference between Vue.js and Angular?
body: Vue is lightweight and progressive, Angular is a full-featured framework with more complexity.

title: How do you create a new Vue project easily?
body: By using Vue CLI (vue create project-name).

title: What is Vue CLI?
body: A command-line tool for scaffolding and managing Vue projects.

title: Can Vue.js work without a build tool?
body: Yes, Vue can be used directly with a <script> tag.

title: What is the default file extension for Vue components?
body: .vue.

title: What are the three sections inside a .vue file?
body: <template>, <script>, <style>.

title: Can Vue components have multiple root elements?
body: No, each component must have exactly one root element.

title: How do you pass dynamic props in Vue?
body: Using :propName="value".

title: How do you handle forms in Vue.js?
body: Using v-model for two-way data binding.

title: What is the Vue DevTools browser extension?
body: A tool to debug and inspect Vue.js applications.

title: Is Vue.js reactive by default?
body: Yes, Vue automatically makes data reactive.

title: What does the key attribute do in Vue lists?
body: Helps Vue track elements when rendering lists with v-for.

title: How does Vue’s reactivity system detect changes?
body: Vue wraps data with getters/setters (Proxy in Vue 3). When data changes, it tracks dependencies and re-renders affected components.

title: What is the difference between ref() and reactive() in Vue 3?
body: ref() makes primitives reactive by wrapping them in an object, while reactive() makes an entire object reactive.

title: When should you use watchers instead of computed properties?
body: Watchers are best for performing side effects or async tasks, while computed is for deriving new reactive values.

title: What is the Virtual DOM’s role in Vue.js?
body: It’s a lightweight copy of the real DOM used to detect changes and apply efficient updates.

title: How do you define a lifecycle hook in the Options API?
body: Example: mounted() { console.log("Mounted!"); }.

title: How do you define a lifecycle hook in the Composition API?
body: Import onMounted, onUpdated, etc. and call them inside setup().

title: What is the use of provide and inject in Vue 3?
body: They allow passing data across deeply nested components without prop drilling.

title: What is a mixin in Vue.js?
body: A mixin is reusable logic that can be included in multiple components.

title: Why are mixins less preferred in Vue 3?
body: They can cause naming conflicts and make code harder to track compared to composables.

title: What are composables in Vue 3?
body: Reusable functions built with the Composition API to share logic across components.

title: How do you register a global component in Vue 3?
body: Use app.component('name', Component) when creating the app instance.

title: What is a dynamic component in Vue?
body: A component rendered using <component :is="compName">.

title: How do you handle props validation in Vue?
body: Define a props object with type and validation rules in the component.

title: What is the difference between $attrs and $props?
body: $props are explicitly declared props, while $attrs contains attributes passed but not declared.

title: How do you emit custom events in Vue 3?
body: Use emit inside setup() or this.$emit('eventName') in Options API.

title: How do you pass arguments with emitted events?
body: Include them as additional parameters in emit, e.g. emit('update', value).

title: What is the difference between v-model in Vue 2 and Vue 3?
body: In Vue 2, it always binds to value/input. In Vue 3, you can bind multiple props with modelValue and update:modelValue.

title: How do you create a custom directive in Vue?
body: Use app.directive('name', { mounted(el, binding) { ... } }).

title: How do you use filters in Vue 3?
body: Filters were removed; instead, use computed properties or methods.

title: How do you lazy-load a component in Vue?
body: Use dynamic import: const Comp = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('./Comp.vue')).

title: How do you optimize performance when rendering large lists?
body: Use v-for with key, pagination, virtualization, or keep-alive.

title: What does the keep-alive component do?
body: It caches inactive components instead of destroying them.

title: What is teleport in Vue 3?
body: It allows rendering a component’s template in a different part of the DOM.

title: How do you share state across multiple components without Vuex?
body: Use provide/inject or lift state up into a common parent.

title: What is the difference between Vuex and Pinia?
body: Pinia is lighter, simpler, supports Composition API, and is the new recommended store.

title: How do you define Vuex state and getters?
body: State is reactive data, getters compute derived state.

title: How do you commit a mutation in Vuex?
body: Use store.commit('mutationName', payload).

title: How do you dispatch an action in Vuex?
body: Use store.dispatch('actionName', payload).

title: What is namespacing in Vuex?
body: It organizes modules into separate namespaces to avoid naming conflicts.

title: What is the purpose of mapState and mapGetters helpers?
body: They map Vuex state and getters to computed properties in components.

title: How do you add navigation guards in Vue Router?
body: Use beforeEach, beforeEnter, or component guards.

title: How do you implement route-based code splitting?
body: Define routes with dynamic import() so code loads only when needed.

title: How do you pass props to a route component?
body: Set props: true in the route configuration.

title: What is dynamic routing in Vue Router?
body: Defining routes with parameters like /user/:id.

title: How do you programmatically navigate in Vue Router?
body: Call $router.push('/path') or $router.replace('/path').

title: What is the difference between history mode and hash mode in Vue Router?
body: Hash mode uses # in URLs, history mode uses the HTML5 history API.

title: How do you handle 404 routes in Vue Router?
body: Add a catch-all route using path: '/:pathMatch(.*)*'.

title: How do you scroll to top on navigation in Vue Router?
body: Define a scrollBehavior function in the router configuration.

title: How do you test Vue components?
body: Use Vue Test Utils with Jest or Vitest.

title: What is snapshot testing in Vue?
body: It ensures a component’s rendered output matches a previously saved snapshot.

title: How do you mock Vuex or Pinia stores in unit tests?
body: Use a mock store object or libraries like @pinia/testing.

title: What is the difference between shallowMount and mount in Vue Test Utils?
body: shallowMount stubs child components, while mount renders the full component tree.

title: What is server-side rendering (SSR) in Vue?
body: Rendering Vue components on the server before sending HTML to the client.

title: Which library is used for SSR in Vue?
body: Nuxt.js is commonly used for SSR with Vue.

title: What is hydration in SSR?
body: The process of attaching Vue reactivity to already server-rendered HTML.

title: What are some common Vue performance optimization techniques?
body: Use computed, memoization, lazy loading, keep-alive, and avoid unnecessary watchers.

title: How do you debug reactivity issues in Vue 3?
body: Use Vue DevTools to inspect reactivity graphs and component updates.

title: How can you optimize bundle size in a Vue.js app?
body: Use code splitting with dynamic imports, tree-shaking unused code, lazy-loading routes/components, and externalizing large libraries via CDN.

title: How does Vue’s reactivity system differ between Vue 2 and Vue 3?
body: Vue 2 uses Object.defineProperty, while Vue 3 uses Proxies, which can handle arrays, nested objects, and property additions better.

title: How would you implement a custom renderer in Vue 3?
body: Use @vue/runtime-core to define createRenderer with custom nodeOps for rendering to environments like canvas or native.

title: What are fragments in Vue 3 and why are they useful?
body: Fragments allow components to return multiple root nodes instead of a single root, improving flexibility.

title: How does Vue handle dependency tracking with the reactivity API?
body: Vue uses effect functions and dependency maps (Dep/ReactiveEffect) to track reads and trigger updates on writes.

title: Explain the difference between shallowReactive and reactive.
body: reactive deeply makes nested properties reactive, while shallowReactive only makes the root reactive.

title: When would you use shallowRef instead of ref?
body: When you don’t want Vue to recursively make nested properties reactive (e.g., for large objects or third-party libs).

title: What is the difference between markRaw and shallowRef?
body: markRaw completely excludes an object from reactivity, while shallowRef only prevents deep reactivity.

title: How does toRefs help when destructuring reactive objects?
body: It preserves reactivity when destructuring properties from a reactive object.

title: How do you avoid prop drilling in a large Vue application?
body: Use provide/inject, Pinia/Vuex, or a global event bus (Vue 2 only).

title: What is tree-shaking and how does Vue 3 support it?
body: Tree-shaking removes unused code. Vue 3 is modular, so bundlers like Rollup/Webpack can eliminate unused APIs.

title: How do Suspense components work in Vue 3?
body: Suspense lets you render a fallback (loading state) while async components or setup functions resolve.

title: How do you handle error boundaries in Vue 3?
body: Use errorCaptured hook in Options API or onErrorCaptured in Composition API.

title: How does Vue differ from React in handling reactivity?
body: Vue is reactive by default with Proxies, while React uses explicit state updates and diffing.

title: How do you optimize a Vue component that re-renders too often?
body: Use v-memo, break it into smaller components, optimize computed properties, or use shallow reactivity.

title: What are custom render functions in Vue?
body: They allow writing templates using JavaScript h() calls instead of .vue templates.

title: How do you extend Vue with plugins?
body: Create an install function (app.use(plugin)) that can register components, directives, or provide global properties.

title: How do you handle circular dependencies in Vue reactivity?
body: Break dependency chains by using computed getters or watchers instead of directly referencing reactive objects.

title: How do you implement dynamic form validation in Vue 3?
body: Use reactive/ref for form state, watchers for validation, or third-party libs like VeeValidate.

title: How do you build a Vue SSR app without Nuxt?
body: Use @vue/server-renderer with a Node.js server and hydrate client-side using the same app.

title: What is the difference between client-only hydration and partial hydration?
body: Client-only hydration hydrates the full HTML, while partial hydration hydrates only interactive parts.

title: How do you implement code-splitting at the component level?
body: Use defineAsyncComponent with dynamic imports for lazy-loading components.

title: What is the difference between setup() and data()?
body: setup() runs before component creation, returning reactive data and logic; data() is an Options API feature returning state only.

title: How do you detect memory leaks in a Vue app?
body: Use Chrome DevTools performance tab, watch for unremoved event listeners, and check Vue DevTools component tree.

title: How do you cancel watchers in Vue 3?
body: Watchers return a cleanup function that can be called to stop tracking.

title: How do you scope provide/inject to a single subtree?
body: Place provide only at the parent component you want as the scope.

title: How do you test Vue 3 composables?
body: Import the function, call it in a test setup with Vue Test Utils or Vitest, and assert its reactive behavior.

title: What is reactivity transform in Vue?
body: A compile-time feature that lets you use refs without .value, simplifying code.

title: How do you handle i18n in Vue 3?
body: Use vue-i18n with createI18n, wrap the app, and use t() for translations inside components.

title: What are renderless components?
body: Components that don’t render UI but expose logic via slots or scoped slots.

title: How do you use teleport with modals?
body: Wrap the modal with <teleport to="body">...</teleport> so it renders outside the main app root.

title: What is hydration mismatch in SSR?
body: When the client-side rendered DOM doesn’t match the server-rendered DOM, causing Vue warnings or errors.

title: How do you solve hydration mismatch issues?
body: Ensure deterministic rendering, avoid random IDs, and match server/client logic.

title: How do you share composables across projects?

title: What challenges arise when scaling large applications with KnockoutJS?

title: How would you optimize performance in a KnockoutJS app with thousands of bindings?

title: Scenario: You notice a memory leak in a Knockout app. What could cause it?

title: What is the difference between pureComputed and regular computed observables?

title: How can you prevent unwanted UI updates when multiple observables change simultaneously?

title: What problems can arise from circular dependencies between computed observables?
body: It can cause infinite loops, stack overflows, and degraded performance if not properly broken with conditionals or deferred computations.

body: By default, it’s synchronous, but async can be managed using promises/async calls combined with observables that update when resolved.

title: What’s the risk of using `ko.toJS()` on a large observable hierarchy?
body: It can be very expensive because it unwraps the entire object tree into raw JS objects, causing performance hits on large datasets.

body: They allow you to extend the behavior of observables, e.g., validation, logging, rate limiting, without modifying core observable logic.

title: Explain how you would debug a binding issue where data doesn’t appear in the UI.

title: How can you manually trigger native browser events using jQuery?
body: Use .trigger() for synthetic events or get(0).dispatchEvent() for native events.

title: Why should jQuery not be used for large-scale modern SPAs?
body: It lacks componentization, state management, and virtual DOM efficiency compared to React, Vue, or Angular.

title: How does .promise() in jQuery animations work?
body: It returns a promise that resolves when all queued animations for selected elements finish.

title: Can you override jQuery’s $ symbol with your own custom alias?
body: Yes, using var jq = jQuery.noConflict(); then call jq('.selector').

title: Explain why document.ready might fire before all images are loaded.
body: Because it only waits for DOM readiness, not full asset loading (unlike window.onload).

title: What’s the difference between .bind('click', fn) and .on('click', fn) in terms of memory usage?
body: .on() attaches fewer handlers via delegation, while .bind() attaches directly to each element, consuming more memory.

title: How does jQuery internally normalize event objects?
body: It wraps native events in a normalized object with consistent properties like which, pageX, pageY.

title: What’s the risk of chaining too many methods in jQuery?
body: Excessive chaining may cause readability issues and multiple DOM reflows if not optimized.

title: How can you create a custom jQuery plugin?
body: Extend $.fn with a function: $.fn.myPlugin = function(){ return this.each(function(){ ... }); }.

title: What’s the difference between .end() and .andSelf() in chaining?
body: .andSelf() (deprecated) included previous set, .end() reverts to previous selection in chain.

title: Why does jQuery recommend against using :visible for performance-heavy apps?
body: :visible forces layout calculations, causing performance overhead.

title: How can you optimize .animate() calls in jQuery?
body: Use queue: false, limit properties, and prefer CSS3 transitions.

title: What is event bubbling and how does .stopPropagation() affect it?
body: Bubbling moves events from child to parent; .stopPropagation() halts this flow.

title: How does .wrapAll() differ from .wrap() in jQuery?
body: .wrapAll() wraps all matched elements together, while .wrap() wraps each element individually.

title: Can you explain the concept of “queue” in jQuery animations?
body: Animations are queued per element; they execute sequentially unless disabled with queue: false.

title: How can you prevent memory leaks in jQuery applications?
body: Use .off() to remove handlers, avoid circular references, use .remove() properly.

title: What is the effect of return false inside a jQuery event handler?
body: It prevents default action and stops propagation (combination of preventDefault + stopPropagation).

title: How does jQuery handle JSONP requests?
body: It dynamically creates a <script> tag with callback parameter to bypass same-origin restrictions.

title: What’s the difference between .map() and .each() in jQuery?
body: .each() iterates without return aggregation, .map() transforms elements and returns a new array/jQuery object.

title: How does .position() differ from .offset() in jQuery?
body: .position() gives coordinates relative to parent, .offset() gives relative to document.

title: What’s the purpose of .finish() in jQuery animations?
body: Immediately completes all queued animations and applies final styles.

title: How does jQuery handle namespaced events?
body: You can bind events with namespaces (.on('click.ns')) and remove them specifically with .off('.ns').

title: Why does .live() perform poorly compared to .on()?
body: .live() attaches events at the document level, checking all events unnecessarily.

title: How does jQuery support cross-domain AJAX requests?
body: By using JSONP or CORS (if supported by server).

title: How do you throttle scroll or resize events with jQuery?
body: Use a custom throttle/debounce function with setTimeout or requestAnimationFrame.

title: What’s the difference between .clone(true) and .clone(false)?
body: .clone(true) copies element with data/events, .clone(false) copies only the element.

title: How does .animate() handle non-numeric CSS properties?
body: Non-numeric values like color require jQuery UI or plugins, since .animate() works with numeric values.

title: What’s the difference between .removeData() and .removeAttr('data-*')?
body: .removeData() clears internal jQuery cache, .removeAttr() removes HTML attribute but not cached value.

title: How do you implement custom animations with easing in jQuery?
body: Use .animate() with easing functions, e.g., swing, linear, or plugins like jQuery UI easing.

title: How does jQuery internally manage chaining?
body: Each method returns a jQuery object (this), allowing continuous method calls.

title: What is the difference between .queue() and .dequeue() in jQuery?
body: .queue() adds functions to execution queue, .dequeue() runs next in queue.

title: How can you detect if an element has an inline event handler in jQuery?
body: Use .attr('onclick') to check, though event delegation won’t show this way.

title: Why is direct DOM caching better than repeated jQuery selectors?
body: Because repeated queries trigger DOM lookups each time, slowing performance.

title: How do you extend jQuery with static utility methods?
body: Add to jQuery object: $.myUtility = function(){ ... }.

title: What is jQuery Mobile mainly used for?
body: Building touch-friendly, responsive mobile web apps.

title: Which attribute defines a page in jQuery Mobile?
body: data-role="page".

title: Fill in the blank: To define a header in jQuery Mobile, use _______.
body: data-role="header".

title: How can you define a footer in jQuery Mobile?
body: Use <div data-role="footer">.

title: Which attribute is used to define a button in jQuery Mobile?
body: data-role="button".

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile is built on top of jQuery Core.
body: True.

title: Which event runs when a page is shown?
body: pageshow.

title: What is the default page transition effect in jQuery Mobile?
body: fade.

title: How do you prevent jQuery Mobile from using Ajax for navigation?
body: Add data-ajax="false" to the link or form.

title: What is the purpose of data-theme in jQuery Mobile?
body: To apply a color theme/style to elements.

title: Which widget is used to display a collapsible panel?
body: data-role="collapsible".

title: How do you create a list view in jQuery Mobile?
body: Use <ul data-role="listview">.

title: What does data-inset="true" do in listviews?
body: Creates inset list with rounded corners.

title: What is the purpose of data-mini="true"?
body: Creates a smaller, more compact UI element.

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile supports responsive grids.
body: True.

title: How do you create a grid layout in jQuery Mobile?
body: Use ui-grid classes like ui-grid-a, ui-block-a.

title: Which attribute is used to group buttons together?
body: data-role="controlgroup".

title: What is the role of data-position="fixed"?
body: Fixes headers/footers at the top or bottom of the screen.

title: How do you create a popup in jQuery Mobile?
body: Use <div data-role="popup">.

title: What does data-rel="dialog" do for a link?
body: Opens the target page as a modal dialog.

title: Which event fires before a page is shown?
body: pagebeforeshow.

title: What is the difference between pageinit and pageshow?
body: pageinit runs once when page is initialized; pageshow runs each time page is displayed.

title: How do you create a navigation bar?
body: Use <div data-role="navbar">.

title: What does data-transition="slide" do?
body: Applies a sliding transition between pages.

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile can load multiple pages inside one HTML file.
body: True.

title: How do you define multiple pages in a single file?
body: Use multiple <div data-role="page"> sections.

title: Which attribute is used to set a back button in a header?
body: data-add-back-btn="true".

title: What is the role of data-icon in buttons?
body: Assigns an icon to the button.

title: How do you refresh a listview after adding items?
body: Call .listview('refresh').

title: What does data-clear-btn="true" do on a text input?
body: Adds a clear (X) button inside the input.

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile works only on Android devices.
body: False, it supports multiple platforms.

title: Which event triggers after Ajax page load is completed?
body: pagecontainerload.

title: How do you disable jQuery Mobile’s auto-enhancement for an element?
body: Use data-role="none".

title: What is the default framework structure used by jQuery Mobile?
body: HTML5 + CSS3 + jQuery Core.

title: How can you create a filterable list?
body: Add data-filter="true" to the listview.

title: What does ui-btn-active class represent?
body: The currently active button state.

title: Which tag is most commonly enhanced into a button by default?
body: <a> tag with href.

title: What is the purpose of data-rel="back"?
body: Navigates back to the previous page.

title: How do you show a loading message programmatically?
body: Use $.mobile.loading('show').

title: Which CSS framework is bundled with jQuery Mobile?
body: Its own theme framework (not Bootstrap).

title: How can you group collapsible panels together?
body: Use <div data-role="collapsible-set">.

title: What does data-role="table" provide in jQuery Mobile?
body: Enhances tables with responsiveness and styling.

title: Which attribute is used to preload a page?
body: data-prefetch.

title: How do you disable page caching in jQuery Mobile?
body: Set data-dom-cache="false".

title: Which event fires when a popup is opened?
body: popupafteropen.

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile supports touch gestures out of the box.
body: True.

title: How do you apply a theme to a specific page?
body: Add data-theme to <div data-role="page">.

title: What is the difference between data-inline="true" and false on buttons?
body: Inline shows buttons side by side; false stacks them.

title: How do you add icons to navbar buttons?
body: Use data-icon attribute in <li><a> elements.

title: What is the purpose of data-rel="popup"?
body: Opens the link target as a popup.

title: What is the difference between pageinit and pagecreate events?
body: pagecreate runs when the DOM structure is enhanced; pageinit runs after initialization is complete.

title: Which method is used to programmatically change pages in jQuery Mobile?
body: $.mobile.changePage().

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile automatically handles deep linking using hash-based URLs.
body: True.

title: What is the purpose of data-dom-cache="true"?
body: Keeps a page in DOM for faster navigation.

title: How can you disable Ajax navigation globally in jQuery Mobile?
body: Set $.mobile.ajaxEnabled = false;.

title: Scenario: You want to open a dialog-style page transition. Which data-rel value do you use?
body: data-rel="dialog".

title: Which event is fired before a popup is closed?
body: popupbeforeclose.

title: What is the purpose of data-role="panel"?
body: Creates a sliding side panel.

title: How can you make a panel display from the right side?
body: Use data-position="right".

title: Fill in the blank: To create a collapsible set, wrap collapsible items inside _______.
body: <div data-role="collapsible-set">.

title: How can you lazy-load content into a page dynamically?
body: Use Ajax + pagecontainer("load", url).

title: What is the difference between data-rel="popup" and data-rel="dialog"?
body: Popup opens inline overlays; dialog opens a full modal page.

title: How do you enhance a select menu into a custom-styled widget?
body: Use <select data-native-menu="false">.

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile supports swipe left/right events.
body: True.

title: Which widget is commonly used for multi-page form navigation?
body: data-role="tabs" or multi-page structure.

title: How can you prevent jQuery Mobile from auto-enhancing form elements?
body: Use data-role="none".

title: What does the ui-content class provide?
body: Applies proper padding and content styling inside a page.

title: How do you change the default theme swatch of a page?
body: Add data-theme="b" (or any swatch letter) to the page.

title: Which function is used to programmatically open a popup?
body: $("#popupID").popup("open");.

title: What does data-dismissible="false" do in popups?
body: Prevents the popup from closing when clicking outside.

title: Scenario: You want a button to submit a form but bypass Ajax. What do you add?
body: data-ajax="false".

title: How can you bind an event only the first time a page is initialized?
body: Use pageinit instead of pageshow.

title: What is the difference between pagecontainerbeforechange and pagecontainerchange?
body: One fires before page change, the other after completion.

title: How do you apply different transitions for page navigation?
body: Use data-transition attribute on the link.

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile supports multiple fixed toolbars in one page.
body: True.

title: What does the attribute data-direction="reverse" do?
body: Reverses the page transition animation.

title: How do you make a collapsible panel expanded by default?
body: Add data-collapsed="false".

title: What is the purpose of data-tap-toggle="false" in fixed toolbars?
body: Prevents toolbars from hiding/showing on tap.

title: How do you load an external page into a panel?
body: Use data-ajax="true" with panel link or load() method.

title: Scenario: You want to highlight the active link in navbar. Which class is applied automatically?
body: ui-btn-active.

title: Which event is triggered when a page fails to load via Ajax?
body: pagecontainerloadfailed.

title: How do you create a responsive table in jQuery Mobile?
body: Add data-role="table" and data-mode="reflow" or columntoggle.

title: What is the difference between columntoggle and reflow table modes?
body: columntoggle allows hiding/showing columns; reflow stacks columns.

title: How do you programmatically close a panel?
body: $("#panelID").panel("close");.

title: What is the purpose of data-split-icon in listview?
body: Defines icon for split button in list item.

title: Which widget provides a multiple-choice toggle option?
body: data-role="flipswitch" or checkbox group.

title: True/False: A jQuery Mobile page can contain multiple panels.
body: True.

title: How do you create a persistent footer across multiple pages?
body: Use data-id on footers with same value.

title: What is the purpose of data-transition="pop"?
body: Opens the page with a pop-up style transition.

title: Which event is fired after panel is opened completely?
body: panelopen.

title: How do you disable history tracking in page navigation?
body: Use changePage({ changeHash: false }).

title: Scenario: You want to preload a dialog before user clicks. Which attribute do you use?
body: data-prefetch="true".

title: How can you dynamically update button text in jQuery Mobile?
body: $("#btnID").text("New Text").button("refresh");.

title: What is the difference between listview("refresh") and listview("destroy")?
body: refresh updates UI; destroy removes enhancements.

title: Which method is used to remove enhancements from an element?
body: .enhanceWithin("destroy") or .removeClass with data-role="none".

title: True/False: jQuery Mobile automatically handles back button navigation.
body: True.

title: How do you configure global settings like theme, transition, or Ajax behavior?
body: Modify $.mobile global configuration object.

title: What is the role of data-filter-placeholder in listview?
body: Customizes placeholder text in filter input.

title: How do you prevent multiple pages from preloading at once?
body: Set $.mobile.pageContainer config options carefully.

title: Which event is triggered after a collapsible expands?
body: collapsibleexpand.

title: Explain the difference between pageinit, pagebeforeshow, and pageshow events in jQuery Mobile.
body: pageinit triggers once when the page is initialized; pagebeforeshow runs before the page transition; pageshow runs after the page is visible.

title: How does jQuery Mobile handle multiple “pages” in a single HTML file?
body: It treats <div data-role="page"> blocks as separate pages and loads/shows them via Ajax navigation.

title: Why is data-ajax="false" sometimes required in jQuery Mobile links or forms?
body: It disables Ajax-based navigation or form submission when server-side full reload is needed.

title: What is the role of the pagecontainer widget in jQuery Mobile?
body: It manages page transitions, navigation history, and page life cycle.

title: How does jQuery Mobile enhance semantic HTML into widgets?
body: By scanning data-role attributes and converting them into styled, interactive UI components.

title: What is the impact of data-role="none" in jQuery Mobile?
body: It prevents auto-enhancement of the element into a widget, keeping raw HTML.

title: How does jQuery Mobile optimize navigation with Ajax?
body: It fetches page fragments via XHR, injects into the DOM, updates history, and transitions smoothly.

title: Scenario: A button in jQuery Mobile is not styled. What is the first thing you should check?
body: Verify if the element has data-role="button" or is inside an auto-enhanced element like <a> or <button>.

title: Explain how theming works in jQuery Mobile.
body: Themes are defined in CSS classes (ui-bar, ui-body, etc.) and applied with data-theme attributes.

title: What is the purpose of data-position="fixed" in headers/footers?
body: It fixes toolbars at top/bottom across page transitions.

title: How do you dynamically refresh a listview after adding new items?
body: Call $('#list').listview('refresh').

title: What are the advantages and drawbacks of using data-prefetch on links?
body: Advantage: Faster navigation by preloading; Drawback: More bandwidth/memory usage.

title: How does jQuery Mobile handle back button navigation?
body: It integrates with browser history API and restores previous pages with Ajax transitions.

title: What is a “multi-page template” in jQuery Mobile?
body: A single HTML file with multiple data-role="page" sections, navigated without full reload.

title: Why is progressive enhancement important in jQuery Mobile?
body: It ensures the site works in basic HTML and progressively upgrades with JS/CSS.

title: What is the difference between popup and dialog in jQuery Mobile?
body: Popups are lightweight overlays, dialogs are full pages styled as modal overlays.

title: How can you disable jQuery Mobile’s auto-initialization?
body: Set $.mobile.autoInitializePage = false before including jQuery Mobile scripts.

title: How does $.mobile.changePage() work?
body: It programmatically navigates to a page with transition options.

title: What are persistent toolbars in jQuery Mobile?
body: Toolbars (header/footer) that remain in place while content pages transition.

title: Why does jQuery Mobile sometimes conflict with other JavaScript frameworks?
body: Because it overrides links, forms, and manipulates DOM aggressively.

title: How do you exclude a page from Ajax navigation in jQuery Mobile?
body: Use data-ajax="false" on the link.

title: What is a “transition” in jQuery Mobile?
body: An animated effect when switching between pages, like slide, fade, flip.

title: How do you handle orientation changes in jQuery Mobile?
body: Use the orientationchange event to adjust layout/UI.

title: Explain the difference between listview and collapsible widgets.
body: Listview creates styled lists with filtering, icons, etc.; collapsible creates expandable/collapsible content.

title: What is the use of $.mobile.loading() function?
body: To show/hide loading message programmatically.

title: How does jQuery Mobile support accessibility?
body: Through ARIA roles, focus management, and semantic markup.

title: What is the effect of data-enhance="false"?
body: Prevents jQuery Mobile from auto-enhancing the element.

title: How can you handle dynamic content injection in jQuery Mobile?
body: Inject HTML and call enhanceWithin() or widget-specific refresh methods.

title: What is the difference between pagecreate and pageinit?
body: pagecreate triggers when DOM for the page is created, pageinit is fired after enhancement.

title: How can you globally disable Ajax navigation in jQuery Mobile?
body: Set $.mobile.ajaxEnabled = false.

title: Explain how filterable works in jQuery Mobile.
body: It adds client-side search filtering to listviews, tables, or custom containers.

title: How does jQuery Mobile handle “progressive enhancement” vs “graceful degradation”?
body: It builds rich UI on top of semantic HTML (enhancement), but degrades to plain HTML when unsupported.

title: Why is enhanceWithin() important for dynamically loaded content?
body: It tells jQuery Mobile to enhance widgets inside a container.

title: How does jQuery Mobile integrate with PhoneGap/Cordova apps?
body: Provides mobile-optimized UI with HTML/JS, while PhoneGap handles native packaging.

title: What is the difference between single-page template and multi-page template?
body: Single-page: one page per HTML file. Multi-page: multiple data-role="page" in one file.

title: How can you preload pages for better performance?
body: Use data-prefetch on links or programmatically load with $.mobile.loadPage().

title: What is the role of data-direction in page transitions?
body: Controls whether the transition animates forward or backward.

title: How does jQuery Mobile enhance form inputs automatically?
body: By applying UI classes and replacing elements with styled widgets.

title: How can you override default transitions in jQuery Mobile?
body: Set $.mobile.defaultPageTransition or use data-transition attribute per link.

title: What are the challenges of SEO with jQuery Mobile?
body: Ajax navigation may hide content from crawlers unless progressive enhancement is used.

title: Why does ui-btn-active persist after navigation?
body: Because jQuery Mobile manages active states for history; may require removeClass manually.

title: What is the use of data-tap-toggle="false" in headers/footers?
body: Prevents toolbars from hiding/showing on tap.

title: How do you programmatically close a popup?
body: Call $('#popup').popup('close').

title: Why is page caching important in jQuery Mobile?
body: Improves navigation speed by avoiding repeated Ajax requests.

title: What is the role of data-transition="none"?
body: Disables animation during navigation.

title: How can you force a full reload of a page instead of Ajax loading?
body: Add rel="external" or data-ajax="false" to the link.

title: What is the difference between pagecontainerbeforeload and pagecontainerload events?
body: beforeload fires before Ajax request; load after content is loaded.

title: How can you disable hash changes in jQuery Mobile navigation?
body: Set $.mobile.hashListeningEnabled = false.

title: How does jQuery Mobile handle fixed toolbars across transitions?
body: Clones/persists toolbar elements and animates only page content.

title: What are the limitations of jQuery Mobile compared to modern frameworks like React Native?
body: Limited componentization, heavy DOM manipulation, weaker state management, and less performance on complex apps.

title: What is React Native?
body: A framework for building mobile apps using JavaScript and React.

title: Who developed React Native?
body: Facebook (Meta).

title: Fill in the blank: React Native is used to build ______ applications.
body: Mobile (iOS and Android).

title: True/False: React Native uses WebView to render apps.
body: False (it uses native components).

title: Which programming language is mainly used in React Native?
body: JavaScript.

title: What is the difference between React and React Native?
body: React is for web apps, React Native is for mobile apps.

title: How do you start a new React Native project?
body: Using npx react-native init ProjectName.

title: Which command runs a React Native app on Android emulator?
body: npx react-native run-android.

title: Scenario: You want to test your React Native app on iOS. Which command do you use?
body: npx react-native run-ios.

title: What is the purpose of Metro bundler in React Native?
body: It bundles and serves JavaScript code to the app.

title: Which tag is the root component in React Native apps?
body: <App />.

title: True/False: React Native supports hot reloading.
body: True.

title: What is the default entry file for a React Native project?
body: index.js.

title: Fill in the blank: React Native uses ______ for styling.
body: JavaScript objects (StyleSheet).

title: Which component is used to display text in React Native?
body: <Text>.

title: Which component is used to create buttons?
body: <Button> or <TouchableOpacity>.

title: What is the difference between <View> and <Text> in React Native?
body: <View> is a container, <Text> is for displaying text.

title: Which component is similar to <div> in React?
body: <View>.

title: How do you apply inline styling in React Native?
body: By passing a style object directly to style prop.

title: What is the use of StyleSheet.create()?
body: It organizes and optimizes styles in React Native.

title: Which component is used for scrolling content?
body: <ScrollView>.

title: What is the difference between <ScrollView> and <FlatList>?
body: <ScrollView> loads all items; <FlatList> renders items lazily.

title: Scenario: You want to render a list of items efficiently. Which component do you use?
body: <FlatList>.

title: Which React Native component is used for handling user input?
body: <TextInput>.

title: Fill in the blank: In React Native, images are displayed using the ______ component.
body: <Image>.

title: How do you handle button press events in React Native?
body: Using onPress prop.

title: Which navigation library is most commonly used in React Native?
body: React Navigation.

title: True/False: React Native can access device APIs like camera and GPS.
body: True.

title: Which tool is used to debug React Native apps?
body: React Native Debugger or Flipper.

title: What is the difference between Expo and React Native CLI?
body: Expo is an SDK for quick development; CLI gives more native control.

title: Which command is used to install a package in React Native?
body: npm install or yarn add.

title: Fill in the blank: React Native bridges ______ and native code.
body: JavaScript.

title: How do you display a loading spinner in React Native?
body: Using <ActivityIndicator>.

title: What does the TouchableOpacity component do?
body: Provides a pressable button with fade effect.

title: Which hook is commonly used in React Native functional components?
body: useState and useEffect.

title: True/False: React Native apps can be published to both Google Play Store and Apple App Store.
body: True.

title: How do you import components from React Native?
body: import { Text, View } from 'react-native';.

title: What is the default port used by Metro bundler?
body: Port 8081.

title: Which file stores the app’s name and entry point?
body: app.json.

title: Scenario: You want to navigate between two screens. Which React Native concept do you use?
body: Navigation (React Navigation library).

title: Fill in the blank: The command to start Metro bundler is npx react-native ______.
body: start.

title: Which platform-specific file is generated for Android builds?
body: .apk or .aab.

title: Which platform-specific file is generated for iOS builds?
body: .ipa.

title: What is the use of Platform module in React Native?
body: To check if app is running on iOS or Android.

title: True/False: React Native supports reusable components.
body: True.

title: Which file is used to configure dependencies in React Native?
body: package.json.

title: What is the purpose of SafeAreaView?
body: Ensures content is rendered within safe display boundaries.

title: How do you refresh the React Native app manually on device?
body: Shake the device → select reload.

title: What is the use of useEffect hook in React Native?
body: To perform side effects like fetching data or setting up listeners.

title: How do you add icons in React Native?
body: By using react-native-vector-icons or other icon libraries.

title: What is the difference between controlled and uncontrolled components in React Native?
body: Controlled components rely on React state, uncontrolled components maintain their own state internally.

title: How does React Native handle styling compared to CSS in web development?
body: It uses JavaScript objects with limited CSS-like properties instead of full CSS.

title: Scenario: You want to persist data locally even after the app restarts. Which library would you use?
body: AsyncStorage or libraries like MMKV.

title: Fill in the blank: useEffect runs after ______.
body: Every render (or when dependencies change).

title: What is the difference between useState and useReducer in React Native?
body: useState is for simple state, useReducer is for complex state logic.

title: True/False: React Native can directly use all React web libraries without modification.
body: False.

title: What is the purpose of Flexbox in React Native?
body: To create responsive layouts using properties like flexDirection, justifyContent, and alignItems.

title: How do you detect the platform (iOS or Android) in React Native?
body: Using the Platform module (Platform.OS).

title: Which lifecycle methods in class components correspond to useEffect in functional components?
body: componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate, and componentWillUnmount.

title: Scenario: You need to show different UI for Android and iOS. How can you do this?
body: Use Platform.OS conditionals or create platform-specific files (.ios.js, .android.js).

title: What is the difference between ScrollView and FlatList?
body: ScrollView renders all items at once, FlatList renders items lazily for better performance.

title: What does the keyExtractor prop in FlatList do?
body: It defines a unique key for each item to help React identify list items.

title: Fill in the blank: TouchableOpacity and TouchableHighlight are examples of ______ components.
body: Touchable/Pressable.

title: What is the purpose of SectionList in React Native?
body: To render grouped lists with section headers.

title: Scenario: You want to animate a button press. Which API would you use?
body: Animated API or Reanimated.

title: What is the difference between controlled TextInput and uncontrolled TextInput?
body: Controlled uses state to manage value, uncontrolled lets the input manage its own value.

title: How can you optimize the performance of a React Native list?
body: Use FlatList with keyExtractor, getItemLayout, initialNumToRender, and memoization.

title: True/False: React Native provides built-in gesture handling.
body: False (needs libraries like react-native-gesture-handler).

title: Which navigation types are supported by React Navigation?
body: Stack, Drawer, Bottom Tab, Top Tab navigation.

title: Scenario: You want to navigate back to the previous screen. Which method do you call?
body: navigation.goBack().

title: What is Android?

title: What is an Activity in Android?

title: What is a Service in Android?
body: A Service is a background component that performs long-running tasks without UI.

body: A Broadcast Receiver listens for system-wide or app-wide broadcast messages and acts upon them.

title: What is a Content Provider?
body: A Content Provider manages app data and allows sharing data between apps securely.

title: What is an Intent in Android?
body: An Intent is a messaging object used to request an action from another component.

title: What is the difference between explicit and implicit intent?
body: Explicit intent specifies the target component; implicit intent allows the system to choose the component.

title: What is the AndroidManifest.xml file?
body: It declares app components, permissions, hardware/software requirements, and app metadata.

title: What are the different types of Android layouts?
body: LinearLayout, RelativeLayout, ConstraintLayout, FrameLayout, TableLayout, and GridLayout.

title: What is the difference between dp and sp in Android?
body: dp (density-independent pixels) is for layout dimensions; sp (scale-independent pixels) is for text size.

title: What is a Fragment in Android?

title: What is a View in Android?

title: What is the difference between Serializable and Parcelable?

title: What is ListView in Android?

title: What is LESS in web development?
body: LESS is a CSS preprocessor that extends CSS with variables, mixins, functions, and nesting to make stylesheet management easier.

title: How do you define a variable in LESS?
body: Use the @ symbol, e.g., @mainColor: #ff0000;.

title: Can you explain what a mixin is in LESS?
body: A mixin is a reusable set of CSS properties that can be included in other selectors.

title: How do you include a mixin in a selector?
body: By writing the mixin name inside the selector, e.g., .rounded-corners();.

title: What is nesting in LESS?
body: Nesting allows you to write CSS selectors inside other selectors to reflect the HTML structure.

title: How do you perform arithmetic operations in LESS?
body: Use +, -, *, /, e.g., width: @baseWidth * 2;.

title: Can LESS use functions? Give an example.
body: Yes, e.g., lighten(@color, 20%) or darken(@color, 10%).

title: What is the difference between LESS and CSS?
body: LESS has variables, mixins, functions, and nesting; CSS does not.

title: How do you import one LESS file into another?
body: Using @import "filename.less";.

title: What is the default file extension for LESS?
body: .less

title: Can LESS be compiled into standard CSS?
body: Yes, using a LESS compiler or build tools like lessc.

title: How do you define a parametric mixin in LESS?
body: By adding parameters in parentheses, e.g., .box-shadow(@x, @y) { box-shadow: @x @y; }.

title: What is a guard in LESS mixins?
body: Guards are conditions to apply mixins only when certain conditions are met, e.g., .mixin (@a) when (@a > 10) { ... }.

title: How can you use colors in LESS variables?
body: Assign color codes to variables, e.g., @primary: #3498db;.

title: What is the advantage of using LESS variables?
body: They allow easy theme management and reusability of values throughout the stylesheet.

title: Can you override a variable in LESS?
body: Yes, define it again later or inside a scope to override the previous value.

title: What is a nested selector?
body: A selector defined inside another selector to show hierarchy, e.g., .menu { .item { color: red; } }.

title: How do you create a reusable button style in LESS?
body: Use a mixin, e.g., .button-style() { padding: 10px; border-radius: 5px; }.

title: How do you perform string operations in LESS?

title: What is Tailwind CSS?

body: Tailwind uses utility classes for styling elements directly, while Bootstrap provides pre-designed components.

body: A utility class is a single-purpose class that applies a specific CSS property, e.g., text-center or bg-red-500.

body: Using npm: npm install tailwindcss and initializing with npx tailwindcss init.

title: How do you apply padding in Tailwind?
body: Use classes like p-4 for padding on all sides or px-4/py-4 for horizontal/vertical padding.

body: Use classes like m-2 for all sides or mt-2, mb-2, ml-2, mr-2 for individual sides.

body: It sets the font size to Tailwind’s predefined extra-large size.

body: Use text-{color}-{shade}, e.g., text-blue-500.

title: How do you change background color in Tailwind?
body: Use bg-{color}-{shade}, e.g., bg-green-300.

title: What does rounded class do?
body: It applies a small border-radius to make corners slightly rounded.

title: How do you make fully rounded elements in Tailwind?
body: Use rounded-full class.

title: How do you make a div take full width?
body: Use w-full.

title: How do you make a div take full height?
body: Use h-full.

body: It applies display: flex to the element.

body: Use italic class.

body: Use uppercase class.

title: What is OpenStack?
body: OpenStack is an open-source cloud computing platform for building public and private clouds  offering compute  networking  and storage services.

title: Name key OpenStack components.
body: Nova (compute)  Neutron (networking)  Cinder (block storage)  Swift (object storage)  Glance (images)  Keystone (identity)  Horizon (dashboard).

title: What is Nova?
body: Nova is the compute service for provisioning and managing virtual machines.

title: What is Neutron?
body: Neutron is the networking service providing APIs for network connectivity  addressing  and policies.

title: What is Cinder?
body: Cinder provides block storage volumes that can be attached to instances.

title: What is Keystone?
body: Keystone is OpenStack’s identity service that handles authentication and service catalog.

title: What is Glance?
body: Glance is the image service used to discover  register  and retrieve virtual machine images.

title: What is Horizon?
body: Horizon is the web-based dashboard that lets users and admins manage OpenStack resources.

title: What is Heat?
body: Heat is the orchestration service used to create and manage stacks via templates.

title: How does OpenStack provide multi-tenancy?
body: Through Projects/Tenants  RBAC  quotas  security groups  and network isolation mechanisms.

title: What are Flavors in OpenStack?
body: Flavors define compute  memory  and disk sizes used to shape instance resource allocation.

title: What are Security Groups?
body: Security Groups are sets of firewall rules applied to instances for network access control.

title: How do you add persistent storage to instances?
body: Attach Cinder volumes or mount Swift-backed storage depending on the use case.

title: How do you upgrade an OpenStack environment?
body: Follow official upgrade guides per release  update services in sequence  run DB migrations  and validate each step in staging.

title: What is Ironic?
body: Ironic provides bare-metal provisioning to manage physical machines like cloud instances.

title: How do you snapshot an instance image?
body: Create a snapshot via Nova or Glance which stores the instance state as an image for reuse.

title: What is LBaaS in OpenStack?
body: Load Balancer as a Service provides managed load balancing functionality for tenant networks.

title: How is HA achieved in OpenStack?
body: Use multiple controller nodes  clustered databases  redundant message queues  and distributed storage replication.

title: What is Placement service?
body: Placement tracks available resources and inventories to make scheduling decisions for workloads.

title: Explain OpenStack architecture.
body: Controllers run API/service endpoints and schedulers  compute nodes run Nova and hypervisors  storage nodes host Cinder/Swift  Keystone handles identity  with message queue and DB backends orchestrating state.

title: How to scale OpenStack for large deployments?
body: Scale horizontally by adding compute/storage nodes  use cells for Nova scaling  shard databases  and scale message queues and telemetry pipelines.

title: How does OpenStack networking work?
body: Neutron uses plugins (ML2)  agents  and drivers to implement VLAN/VXLAN/GRE overlays  provider networks  routers  and security groups.

title: How to secure an OpenStack deployment?
body: Enable TLS for APIs  enforce Keystone RBAC  isolate projects with security groups and networks  harden images  and rotate credentials.

title: How to integrate Kubernetes with OpenStack?
body: Use Magnum for managed k8s or deploy k8s on Nova VMs using Cinder for persistent volumes and Neutron for networking.

title: How to troubleshoot scheduler or placement issues?
body: Check scheduler logs  placement API responses  resource inventories  and database consistency; validate host aggregates and resource providers.

title: How to implement billing/chargeback in OpenStack?
body: Collect usage via telemetry (Ceilometer/Gnocchi)  aggregate metrics  and feed into billing engines or custom chargeback pipelines.

title: What is the role of message queue and DB in OpenStack?
body: They persist state and coordinate services; the message queue (Rabbit/Zaqar) transports RPC  DB stores authoritative service state.

title: How to optimize OpenStack storage performance?
body: Tune backend storage (Ceph  LVM)  configure optimal replication/erasure coding  use SSDs for hot data  and tune IO scheduler and caching.

title: What is VMware vSphere?
body: VMware vSphere is a virtualization platform including ESXi hypervisor and vCenter for centralized management of virtualized infrastructure.

title: What is ESXi?
body: ESXi is a Type-1 bare-metal hypervisor that runs virtual machines directly on host hardware.

title: What is vCenter Server?
body: vCenter Server centrally manages multiple ESXi hosts  VMs  clusters  and provides features like HA and DRS.

title: What is a datastore?
body: A datastore is a storage container (VMFS or NFS) that holds VM files  disks  and templates.

title: What is vMotion?
body: vMotion enables live migration of running VMs between ESXi hosts without downtime.

title: What is VMware HA?
body: HA (High Availability) restarts VMs on other hosts if a host fails  minimizing downtime.

title: What is DRS?
body: DRS (Distributed Resource Scheduler) automatically balances VM workloads across hosts for optimal resource usage.

title: What is VMware Tools?
body: VMware Tools is a suite of utilities installed inside guest OSes to improve performance and management.

title: What is a VM snapshot?
body: A snapshot captures a point-in-time state of a VM for backup or rollback purposes.

title: What is a vSphere cluster?
body: A vSphere cluster groups ESXi hosts together for shared resource management and services like HA and DRS.

title: What is a resource pool?
body: Resource pools are logical containers to allocate CPU and memory shares and limits among groups of VMs.

title: What is Storage vMotion?
body: Storage vMotion migrates VM disk files between datastores while the VM is running.

title: What is vCenter Server Appliance (VCSA)?
body: VCSA is the appliance distribution of vCenter based on a preconfigured Linux appliance (Photon OS).

title: What is Content Library?
body: Content Library stores VM templates  ISO images  and scripts centrally for distribution across vCenter instances.

title: How do you patch ESXi hosts?
body: Use VMware Lifecycle Manager (formerly VUM) to stage and remediate ESXi hosts with patches and upgrades.

title: What is vSAN?
body: vSAN is VMware’s software-defined storage that pools local disks across hosts to present shared datastore.

title: How to back up vCenter and VMs?
body: Use vSphere APIs with backup solutions  snapshot-based backups  or third-party backup products supporting VADP.

title: What are Host Profiles?
body: Host Profiles capture host configuration baselines to enforce consistent host configurations across clusters.

title: How does vSphere integrate with public clouds?
body: Via VMware Cloud on AWS  hybrid connectors  APIs  and vSphere replication to extend or migrate workloads.

title: Explain vSphere networking components.
body: vSphere networking includes vSwitch (vSS)  vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS)  port groups  NIC teaming  VLAN tagging  and traffic shaping for VM networking.

title: How to secure vSphere environment?
body: Use role-based access control  enable secure boot/VM encryption  use NSX microsegmentation  and secure vCenter endpoints with TLS and MFA.

title: What is HA isolation response and heartbeat?
body: HA uses network/datastore heartbeats to detect host isolation; isolation response determines VM restart behavior if host is isolated.

title: How to troubleshoot vMotion issues?
body: Check network MTU and connectivity  shared storage accessibility  vSphere Compatibility/CPU features (EVC)  and vCenter/vMotion logs.

title: How to scale vCenter for enterprise?
body: Use proper sizing  distributed vCenter architecture or linked mode  scale DB and backup  and follow VMware performance guidelines.

title: Explain Storage I/O Control (SIOC).
body: SIOC prioritizes storage I/O across VMs when datastore latency exceeds thresholds using I/O shares to distribute throughput.

title: How to configure DRS rules?
body: Use VM-Host affinity/anti-affinity and VM-VM rules to control placement and maintain compliance with licensing or topology needs.

title: What is NSX and how does it integrate with vSphere?
body: NSX is VMware’s network virtualization platform providing L2-L7 services and integrates with vCenter and distributed switching for microsegmentation.

title: How to remediate host profile compliance drift?
body: Compare host to profile  review noncompliant items  and apply remediation which updates host config to match profile.

title: How to design a multi-tenant secure vSphere environment?
body: Use separate resource pools  role-based access  network isolation with NSX  dedicated datastores or encryption  and monitor via logging and alerts.
