title: Explain strides and how they enable views like transpose and slicing without copies.
body: Strides are byte steps per axis; changing strides (via transpose/slicing) reinterprets the same buffer in new shapes without copying.

title: How would you implement a rolling window operation using stride tricks?
body: Use numpy.lib.stride_tricks.as_strided to expose sliding windows, then reduce; guard with correct shape/stride and avoid out-of-bounds.

title: When does broadcasting create large temporary arrays and how to avoid it?
body: Broadcasting with large expanded dims (e.g., (N,1)*(1,M)) creates N×M temporaries; avoid by using einsum, matmul, or reduce over axes.

title: How do you diagnose hidden copies that hurt performance?
body: Check a.flags, a.base, np.may_share_memory, and use memory profiling; watch for fancy indexing which returns copies.

title: Explain cache locality and how memory layout impacts vectorized speed.
body: Row-major access to contiguous blocks improves cache hits; choose layouts (C/F) and loop orders to match access pattern.

title: How to ensure BLAS uses multiple threads when calling np.dot / @?
body: Install a multithreaded BLAS (MKL/OpenBLAS) and set OMP_NUM_THREADS/MKL_NUM_THREADS; verify via np.show_config or timing.

title: Why is summing float32 large arrays inaccurate and how to improve stability?
body: Float32 has limited mantissa; sum in float64 or use pairwise summation to reduce error accumulation.

title: How to perform stable summation (Kahan/ pairwise) in NumPy?
body: Use np.add.reduce(a, dtype=np.float64) or math.fsum on Python side; for very large arrays use blockwise pairwise reduce.

title: When do you prefer einsum over chained operations? Give a rationale.
body: When replacing multiple transposes/reshapes and elementwise ops, einsum can be clearer and avoids temporaries.

title: Design a vectorized approach to compute pairwise cosine similarity for rows of a matrix.
body: Normalize rows (X /= ||X||), then use X @ X.T (or einsum) while controlling memory by chunking if needed.

title: Explain views vs. copies interactions with fancy indexing and boolean masks.
body: Fancy/boolean indexing always copies; only basic slicing gives views—so chained fancy ops can hide costly copies.

title: How do you build a read-only view and why would you use it?
body: v = A.view(); v.flags.writeable = False; protects data and catches unintended writes.

title: What are the pitfalls of using as_strided?
body: It can create views that alias invalid memory; safe only when strides are correct within the original buffer bounds.

title: How do you detect and fix negative/overlapping strides breaking downstream code?
body: Check a.strides for negatives/overlaps, materialize with a.copy() if consumers require contiguous positive strides.

title: Explain alignment and itemsize and why misalignment can degrade performance.
body: Dtype alignment affects vectorized loads/stores; inspect with a.dtype.alignment and a.dtype.fields offsets.

title: How to compute gradient/finite differences without loops on multi-dim arrays?
body: Use np.diff along axes or convolution kernels; for N-D, np.gradient computes finite differences vectorized.

title: How to implement batched matrix multiply efficiently without explicit Python loops?
body: Reshape to batches and use @ or einsum (e.g., np.matmul for (B,N,K)@(B,K,M)); avoid Python loops.

title: How to preallocate and write into output buffers using ufuncs and out= to avoid allocations?

title: How do you use broadcasting + where to implement branchless logic?
body: y = np.where(cond, y1, y2) or ufunc(..., where=cond) to avoid branches and temporaries.

title: When would you prefer memory-mapping (memmap) over loading into RAM?
body: When arrays exceed RAM or random access is needed without loading fully; memmap maps files to memory pages.

title: How do you stream-process a file larger than RAM into chunked NumPy ops?
body: Iterate in chunks with np.fromfile / memmap or buffered readers; process and write out results per chunk.

body: Use memory-mapped arrays, cache frequently used small metadata in memory, and minimize disk I/O by batching reads.

title: Explain difference between stable and unstable sorts; when do you need kind='stable'?
body: Stable keeps relative order of equal keys; use kind="stable" when secondary keys or deterministic outputs matter.

title: How to compute top-k efficiently on huge arrays?
body: Use np.argpartition(a, -k)[-k:] then partial sort; avoids full O(n log n) sort.

title: How to find the N largest elements per row without sorting whole rows?
body: Use argpartition per row on negatives, gather with take_along_axis for top-k per row.

body: Combine chained where/ufuncs; or use piecewise vectorization with np.select to avoid Python loops.

title: How to compute rolling quantiles approximately with limited memory?
body: Approximate with t-digest (external) or blockwise selection + argpartition; pure NumPy may require chunking + merge.

body: Hash rows (e.g., view as void and use np.unique) and dedupe by tolerance with rounding or lexsort+diff thresholds.

title: How to use searchsorted for fast join-like operations between sorted arrays?
body: Use searchsorted to align keys to positions in another sorted array, then fancy-index to join corresponding values.

title: How to accelerate a custom numerical loop: choices between vectorize, numba, Cython, or C-extensions?
body: Prefer numba/Cython/C for hot loops; vectorize/frompyfunc are convenience wrappers and slower than real ufuncs.

title: What are the rules for writeable flags and how to avoid “assignment destination is read-only”?
body: Writeability is tracked by the flags; views from read-only buffers or memmaps may be non-writeable—copy if you must assign.

body: Implement in C/Cython/numba with nopython and nogil or use Py_UFunc API to make true ufuncs that release the GIL.

title: How to control threadpool interference between NumPy, BLAS, and joblib in a pipeline?
body: Coordinate thread counts across libs (set env vars, use threadpoolctl/joblib) to avoid oversubscription.

title: How to detect and avoid temporary arrays in chained expressions (fusion)?
body: Fuse operations manually with einsum or use in-place operations; break chains to reuse buffers.

title: What’s the difference between fit, transform, and fit_transform?
body: fit learns parameters; transform applies; fit_transform does both on the same data.

title: What’s the difference between predict and predict_proba?
body: predict returns labels/values; predict_proba returns class probabilities.

title: How do you do a simple train/validation/test split?
body: Split train/test, then split part of train into validation.

title: How do you quickly get a baseline with a dummy classifier?
body: DummyClassifier(strategy="most_frequent"/"stratified")

title: How do you check estimator parameters and default values?
body: estimator.get_params()

title: How do you print scikit-learn version?
body: import sklearn; sklearn.__version__

title: Explain k-fold vs stratified k-fold and when to use each.
body: KFold splits by index; StratifiedKFold preserves class ratios—use it for classification, especially with imbalance.

title: How does cross_val_score differ from cross_validate?
body: cross_val_score returns a single score array; cross_validate can return multiple metrics and timings.

title: How do you build a numeric+categorical preprocessing pipeline with scaling, imputation, and OHE?
body: ColumnTransformer + Pipeline: impute+scale numeric; impute+one-hot categorical; then estimator.

title: How do you do nested CV for unbiased model selection?
body: Run inner CV for hyperparameter tuning and outer CV for unbiased performance estimates.

title: When would you use GroupKFold or GroupShuffleSplit?
body: Use when samples share a group (same user/session); groups never split across folds.

title: How do you prevent data leakage in time series?
body: Use temporal splits; never shuffle across time; fit scalers/imputers only on past windows.

title: How do you perform time-series CV correctly?
body: TimeSeriesSplit (or custom splits) preserving order and expanding/rolling windows.

title: How do you tune hyperparameters inside a Pipeline without leakage?
body: Put transformers and estimator inside a single Pipeline and pass param grid with step__param names.

title: Compare GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV trade-offs.
body: Grid: exhaustive, expensive; Randomized: samples combos, often finds good configs faster on large spaces.

title: How do you limit search time per model during tuning?
body: Use TimeLimit/Timeout callbacks indirectly (e.g., HalvingGridSearchCV) or restrict n_iter and CV folds; or wrap with job timeouts.

title: How do you tune threshold for maximum F1 on validation data?
body: Use decision_function/proba on validation set; pick threshold maximizing F1 (or cost) via precision_recall_curve.

title: How do you get a PR curve and average precision?
body: precision_recall_curve + average_precision_score; plot PR curve.

title: How do you calibrate classifier probabilities?
body: CalibratedClassifierCV with sigmoid/isotonic on a validation split.

title: How do you handle severe class imbalance during training?
body: Resample (SMOTE/etc.), use class_weight="balanced", focal-like losses (outside sklearn), and threshold tuning.

title: How do you compute class weights programmatically?
body: compute_class_weight("balanced", classes=np.unique(y), y=y)

title: How do you evaluate with macro vs micro averaging?
body: Macro treats classes equally; micro aggregates over all instances.

title: How do you do multi-label evaluation (subset accuracy, F1)?
body: Use metrics for multi-label (f1_score with average="samples"/"micro") and subset_accuracy_score.

title: How do you evaluate regression beyond RMSE (MAE, R2, MAPE)?
body: Report MAE, R2, MAPE; use cross_validate with multiple scorings.

title: How do you perform permutation feature importance?
body: permutation_importance(estimator, X, y, n_repeats=...)

title: How do you compute SHAP-like or PDP/ICE with scikit-learn tooling?
body: PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator / ICE for tree/GBM/linear models.

title: How do you select features via univariate tests?
body: SelectKBest/SelectPercentile with f_classif, mutual_info, etc.

title: How do you use model-based feature selection?
body: SelectFromModel with L1 models or tree importances.

title: When and how to use RFE/RFECV?
body: RFE recursively removes weakest features; RFECV finds optimal count via CV.

title: How do you prevent target/feature leakage in preprocessing?
body: Fit preprocessing only on train folds; never peek at the target in transforms.

title: How do you persist a full Pipeline cleanly for production?
body: Dump the Pipeline with joblib; load and call predict—no separate preprocessing code.

title: How do you create a custom Transformer (fit/transform)?
body: Subclass BaseEstimator + TransformerMixin; implement fit (return self) and transform.

title: How do you create a custom scorer for GridSearch?
body: make_scorer(custom_func, greater_is_better=..., needs_proba=...)

title: How do you add custom steps to ColumnTransformer for specific columns?
body: Use ColumnTransformer with tuples selecting specific column names or indices.

title: How do you combine multiple feature extractors in parallel?
body: FeatureUnion or ColumnTransformer with parallel branches.

title: Explain make_pipeline / make_column_selector convenience.
body: make_pipeline auto-names steps; make_column_selector selects by dtype/regex.

title: How do you stack models (classifiers/regressors) natively?
body: StackingClassifier/StackingRegressor with cross-validated meta-features.

title: Explain Voting vs Stacking: when to choose which?
body: Voting averages (hard/soft) predictions; Stacking learns a meta-model—prefer stacking when base models are diverse.

title: How do you generate out-of-fold predictions for stacking safely?
body: Use cross_val_predict with method="predict_proba"/"decision_function" for OOF features.

title: How do you tune an SVM with RBF kernel (C, gamma)?
body: Search C and gamma on log-scale; scale features; use StratifiedKFold CV.

title: How do you scale/center sparse input safely?
body: Use MaxAbsScaler/StandardScaler(with_mean=False) to keep sparsity.

title: When to prefer linear models with elastic net vs tree ensembles?
body: High-dimensional linear + elastic net for interpretability/speed; trees/GBMs for non-linear, interaction-heavy data.

title: How do you do polynomial feature expansion within a Pipeline?
body: PolynomialFeatures inside Pipeline + scaler + linear model or kernel methods.

title: How do you evaluate a classifier under heavy class skew (metrics + CV)?
body: Use PR-AUC, F1, balanced accuracy; stratified CV and proper class weights.

title: How do you build a leakage-free text pipeline (Tfidf + LinearSVC)?
body: Pipeline([("tfidf", TfidfVectorizer()), ("clf", LinearSVC())]); fit only on train.

title: When should you use partial_fit (online learning)?
body: For SGDClassifier, Perceptron, NB, MiniBatchKMeans—when data streams or doesn’t fit RAM.

title: How do you warm_start incremental estimators?
body: Set warm_start=True (or call partial_fit) to continue training from previous state.

title: How do you implement early stopping in gradient boosting?
body: HistGradientBoosting/GradientBoosting with early_stopping=True or monitor via validation.

title: How do you avoid multi-collinearity issues in linear models?
body: Drop collinear features, use regularization (ridge/elastic net), or PCA.

title: How do you control randomness across CV, models, and NumPy?
body: Set all random_state, seed NumPy, and pass random_state down CV splitters and models.

title: How do you profile fit/predict time and memory?
body: Use cross_validate(return_train_score, scoring) and memory profilers; check estimator attributes (n_features_in_, n_iter_).

title: How do you cap CPU threads from scikit-learn/BLAS during runs?
body: Set env vars (e.g., OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS) or threadpoolctl to cap threads.

title: How do you make your training deterministic across platforms?
body: Pin versions, seeds, single-thread BLAS; avoid nondeterministic algorithms.

title: How do you debug “non-converged” warnings in solvers?
body: Increase max_iter, scale features, relax tol, or change solver; inspect n_iter_.

title: How do you catch and fix “Found input variables with inconsistent numbers of samples”?
body: Check X and y shapes, lengths; align indices; ensure no ragged lists; validate in fit.

title: Design a full leakage-proof modeling pipeline for mixed types (num/cat/text) with CV and tuning.
body: Use ColumnTransformer: (num: SimpleImputer+StandardScaler), (cat: OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")), (text: TfidfVectorizer via Pipeline). Wrap the whole thing in Pipeline and tune via Grid/RandomizedSearch with StratifiedKFold; fit transformers only on training folds.

title: Propose a robust approach to feature hashing for high-cardinality categories within a Pipeline.
body: Use HashingEncoder-style approach with sklearn’s FeatureHasher inside a ColumnTransformer branch; keep sparse output and ensure deterministic n_features_out.

title: Build a custom target encoder that avoids leakage across folds.
body: Create a TargetEncoder transformer that in fit computes per-category means via CV folds (out-of-fold stats); in transform, map categories; fallback for unknowns.

title: Design a nested CV with grouped splits and early stopping safe for time series.
body: Use GroupTimeSeriesSplit with embargo/blackout windows; place early-stopping models (e.g., HistGBDT) inside Pipeline and tune on inner splits.

title: How do you tune and evaluate models with severe label shift between train and deployment?
body: Reweight samples (class_weight or sample_weight), tune thresholds on a validation reflecting deployment prior; use importance weighting or domain adaptation in evaluation.

title: Construct a cost-sensitive classifier that optimizes a custom utility function.
body: Define a custom scorer via make_scorer that computes expected utility from confusion matrix using business costs; optimize with Grid/RandomizedSearchCV.

title: Implement custom metrics that require group awareness (per-user recall then macro).
body: Write a scorer that groups by user, computes recall per user, then returns macro mean; pass greater_is_better=True.

title: Create a custom transformer that uses y during fit but is safe in CV.
body: Custom transformer accepting y in fit(X,y) to learn encodings, but transform(X) ignores y; always fit inside CV folds to avoid leakage.

title: Calibrate an imbalanced classifier while preserving ranking for thresholding.
body: Fit CalibratedClassifierCV on a held-out fold; use sigmoid/isotonic; use probabilities for threshold selection while keeping rank monotonicity.

title: Devise a model monitoring plan (data drift, PSI, performance decay) for sklearn models.
body: Track data drift (KS/PSI), feature ranges, missingness, and performance (AUC/RMSE) with periodic re-evaluation; store baselines and alert on deltas.

title: Implement a robust imputer that learns per-segment statistics (e.g., by region).
body: Wrap SimpleImputer per region in ColumnTransformer using remainder="drop"; or write a transformer that groups by region and stores stats for transform.

title: Create a multi-output regression Pipeline with different preprocessors per target.
body: Use MultiOutputRegressor with separate pipelines per target or a shared preprocessing ColumnTransformer plus multi-output estimator.

title: Design a multilabel text classification system with TF-IDF, linear model, and threshold tuning.
body: Pipeline([("tfidf", TfidfVectorizer()) , ("clf", OneVsRestClassifier(LinearSVC()))]); tune per-label thresholds via precision-recall trade-off on validation.

title: Build a stacking ensemble with heterogeneous base learners and a regularized meta-learner.
body: StackingClassifier/Regressor with base models (linear, trees, SVM) and a L2-regularized logistic/linear meta-learner using cross_val_predict for OOF features.

title: Explain how to avoid double-dipping when stacking or target encoding.
body: Compute target encodings and meta-features strictly out-of-fold; never fit on full data before generating training features.

title: Propose a scalable permutation importance procedure under tight latency budgets.
body: Run permutation_importance on a validation set with n_repeats small; subsample features/rows; cache predictions to limit calls.

title: Implement PDP/ICE diagnostics for tree ensembles in production.
body: PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator for features of interest; subsample rows; cache estimator predictions.

title: Execute SHAP-like global explanations using model-agnostic tools around sklearn.
body: Use shap (external) or model-agnostic permutation importance + PDP/ICE for global/local views; document limitations.

title: Construct a fairness evaluation harness (EO/DP metrics) around sklearn predictions.
body: Compute equalized odds / demographic parity from predictions; slice by sensitive attribute and report delta metrics; integrate into CI.

title: Devise a stratified CV strategy for multilabel tasks.
body: Use iterative stratification or label powerset for stratified multilabel; otherwise use repeated KFold with macro/micro metrics.

title: Implement a confidence/uncertainty score for non-probabilistic classifiers.
body: For SVC/LinearSVC, use decision_function magnitude as confidence; calibrate if needed; report confidence intervals via bootstrap.

title: Design a custom cross-validator that respects time gaps and blackout windows.
body: Subclass BaseCrossValidator: ensure splits respect min gaps between train/test; add embargo around events.

title: Engineer a feature store-like fit/transform contract using ColumnTransformer.
body: Centralize feature building in ColumnTransformer; save fitted transformer with model to ensure identical transforms at inference.

title: Create a safe serializer/versioner for Pipelines across Python/sklearn upgrades.
body: Serialize with joblib plus a manifest (versions, schema); include a compatibility check and canary tests on load.

title: Build a robust outlier handling and winsorization step with rollback.
body: Compute IQR bounds per group; clip/winsorize; keep original in parallel column for rollback/audit.

title: Design a scalable top-k recommendation (implicit feedback) using sklearn-compatible pieces.
body: Use implicit MF outside sklearn or approximate with nearest neighbors; for sklearn-compatibility, treat as ranking with pairwise models or SGD with implicit feedback labels.

title: Create a semi-supervised learning flow (label propagation/self-training) with safeguards.
body: SelfTrainingClassifier / LabelPropagation with confidence thresholds; always validate on labeled set and monitor label noise.

title: Engineer a data-centric evaluation grid (slices by geography/segment) in CV.
body: Define CV splitters by slice (region, cohort); aggregate scores per slice; fail if weak slices regress.

title: Build a partial-fit online training service with backpressure and checkpoints.
body: Use partial_fit models (SGDClassifier, Perceptron, MiniBatchKMeans); checkpoint every N batches; apply backpressure on input queue.

title: Implement batched inference with memory-mapping and constrained threads.
body: Load batches via memory-map/Arrow, run predict in chunks, set threadpool limits (threadpoolctl) to avoid oversubscription.

title: Devise a hyperparameter search that mixes Bayesian/global + local fine-tuning (within sklearn APIs).
body: Combine HalvingGridSearchCV for coarse search, then local Grid around the incumbent’s neighborhood; wrap both with same Pipeline.

title: Construct a reproducibility recipe (env pinning, seeds, threads) for a whole org.
body: Freeze package versions, set seeds, set MKL/OMP threads, record data hashes; enforce in CI.

title: Design a policy for handling unknown categories at inference (avoid crashes).
body: Use OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore") or OrdinalEncoder with unknown_value; add robust default buckets in encoders.

title: Implement numeric stability guardrails for scaling/standardization at extreme values.
body: Clip/scale robustly (RobustScaler/QuantileTransformer); guard against inf/NaN; use np.isfinite checks; add eps in denominators.

title: Build a robust timeseries regression with lag features and leakage-safe CV.
body: Lag features with a leak-safe TimeSeriesSplit; keep all transforms inside Pipeline; avoid using future info (rolling with closed="left").

title: Engineer a hierarchical model (per-store, per-region) with shared/global effects in sklearn style.
body: Use ColumnTransformer with per-level pipelines; approximate hierarchy via one-hot of region and interaction features, or fit per-group models via MultiOutput wrappers.

title: Create a custom scorer optimizing recall@k or profit@k using decision scores.
body: Define make_scorer that computes recall@k or profit using decision scores sorted per case; integrate into GridSearchCV.

title: Implement a large-scale sparse linear model with hashing + SGD and early stopping.
body: Build Pipeline with HashingVectorizer/FeatureHasher → SGDClassifier(loss="log") with early_stopping=True on validation split.

title: Design a principled threshold selection policy tied to business costs.
body: Given costs (FP, FN), compute threshold maximizing expected profit on validation; codify as a function and log chosen threshold.

title: Create a counterfactual evaluation using cross_val_predict and propensity weighting.
body: Use cross_val_predict to get OOF predictions; compute IPS/propensity weights; estimate counterfactual metrics.

title: Implement a production A/B switch between models with canary and rollback using sklearn objects.
body: Wrap models behind a facade that can route % of traffic to a challenger; monitor metrics; rollback if SLOs breach.

title: Engineer a memory-aware Pipeline for 100M rows (chunked fit/transform).
body: Chunked preprocessing with partial transformers (incremental fit) or stateless transforms; write intermediate parquet; keep memory footprint bounded.

title: Build an interpretable GBM via monotonic constraints and feature grouping (sklearn-compatible).
body: Use external library (e.g., LightGBM) for monotonic constraints; if staying sklearn-compatible, enforce monotonic transforms and grouped features, validate with PDP monotonicity checks.

title: Design a test suite for Pipelines: invariants, serialization, drift checks.
body: Pytest suite: check invariants (no NaN after transform), serialization round-trip, drift thresholds, and stable metrics on fixtures.

title: Create a robust join-merging preprocessor step with key validation inside a Pipeline.
body: Custom transformer that validates/join-merges on keys; raises on duplicates/missing; keeps schema in df.attrs.

title: Implement out-of-distribution detection wrapper around any sklearn classifier.
body: Wrap classifier; at predict time compute embedding distances or score entropy; flag low-confidence/OOD samples.

title: Build a meta-estimator that retries with different imputers on failure.
body: Meta-estimator tries SimpleImputer(mean) then (median); falls back to KNNImputer if validation score improves.

title: Create an ensemble that mixes calibrated and uncalibrated classifiers coherently.
body: Blend calibrated (for probability tasks) with raw margin-based models; weight by calibration loss on validation.

title: Design a Monte-Carlo CV to quantify score uncertainty beyond k-fold.
body: Shuffle-split many random folds, compute mean±CI; useful when dataset is small or unstable.

title: Build a minimal MLOps loop (train → validate → package → monitor) solely with sklearn + stdlib.
body: Use sklearn Pipeline + stdlib (argparse/logging/joblib); package wheel; export model card; monitor with scheduled batch jobs.

title: What is TensorFlow and what kinds of problems is it used for?
body: An open-source deep learning library by Google for building, training, and deploying ML/DL models.

title: How do you install TensorFlow for CPU-only vs GPU?
body: pip install tensorflow (CPU); pip install tensorflow-gpu (legacy) or use unified tf with GPU drivers.

title: Explain the difference between TensorFlow and Keras.
body: Keras is a high-level API integrated with TensorFlow; TensorFlow is the full ML framework.

title: How do you import TensorFlow and check its version?
body: import tensorflow as tf; print(tf.__version__)

title: What does eager execution mean in TensorFlow?
body: Immediate execution of ops (like Python functions) instead of building a static graph.

title: How do you create a constant tensor and a variable tensor?
body: tf.constant(...) creates immutable; tf.Variable(...) creates mutable, trainable parameters.

title: What is the purpose of `tf.data.Dataset`?
body: Efficient data loading/streaming pipelines for model training.

title: How do you batch and shuffle a dataset with `tf.data`?
body: dataset.shuffle(buffer).batch(batch_size)

title: What is a `Sequential` model in Keras and when is it appropriate?
body: A simple stack of layers; good when each layer feeds only into the next.

title: How do you add layers to a Keras model?
body: By passing layers list into Sequential() or model.add().

title: What are common activation functions you’d use in Keras layers?
body: Relu, Sigmoid, Softmax, Tanh, etc.

title: How do you compile a Keras model (which arguments matter)?
body: Specify optimizer, loss, and metrics: model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="binary_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])

title: How do you fit a model and track training metrics?
body: model.fit(X_train, y_train, epochs=..., batch_size=..., validation_data=...)

title: How do you evaluate a model and get predictions?
body: model.evaluate(X_test, y_test); model.predict(X_test)

title: What is a callback in Keras and name a few common callbacks?
body: Objects triggered during training: EarlyStopping, ModelCheckpoint, TensorBoard, ReduceLROnPlateau.

title: How do you save and load a Keras model?
body: model.save("path"); tf.keras.models.load_model("path")

title: What is a `SavedModel`?
body: TensorFlow’s portable serialization format with graph + weights + signatures.

title: How do you load image data efficiently for training?
body: Use image_dataset_from_directory, tf.data pipelines, or tf.keras.preprocessing.

title: What’s the difference between `model.summary()` and `model.get_config()`?
body: summary shows layer architecture; get_config shows model’s configuration dictionary.

title: How do you set a random seed for reproducibility in TensorFlow/Keras?
body: tf.random.set_seed(42); np.random.seed(42) for reproducibility.

title: What is a loss function and give two examples for classification?
body: Functions measuring error between predictions and targets; e.g., binary_crossentropy, categorical_crossentropy.

title: What’s the difference between accuracy and loss?
body: Loss quantifies error, accuracy measures correctness; you can have low loss but not perfect accuracy.

title: How do you use `tf.one_hot` and when is it needed?
body: Convert integer labels to one-hot encodings for classification models.

title: What optimizer would you start with for many problems and why?
body: Adam optimizer; balances speed, adaptivity, and robustness.

title: What is `tf.GradientTape` used for?
body: Record operations to compute gradients for autodiff and custom training loops.

title: How do you freeze layers when fine-tuning a pretrained model?
body: Set layer.trainable=False to stop weights updating.

title: What is transfer learning in Keras?
body: Reusing pretrained weights on a new problem, fine-tuning only some layers.

title: How do you monitor overfitting during training?
body: Track validation loss/metrics; use early stopping or plot training vs validation curves.

title: What is the purpose of validation data in `model.fit`?
body: To measure generalization on unseen data while training.

title: Compare eager execution with graph mode (`@tf.function`); what are the trade-offs?
body: Eager: executes immediately, intuitive but slower; Graph (@tf.function): optimized, faster, portable.

title: When and why would you wrap code with `@tf.function` (AutoGraph)?
body: Use for performance-critical, repeated code; lets TF optimize with graph execution.

title: Explain the Keras functional API and its benefits over `Sequential`.
body: Define DAG of layers/ops explicitly, supports multiple inputs/outputs, more flexible.

title: How do you build a custom `tf.keras.layers.Layer`? What methods do you override?
body: Subclass tf.keras.layers.Layer; override __init__, build, call methods.

title: How do you create a custom loss or metric in Keras?
body: Subclass tf.keras.losses.Loss/metrics.Metric or define a function(y_true,y_pred).

title: Explain how `tf.GradientTape` works with multiple tapes and persistent mode.
body: GradientTape records ops; persistent=True allows multiple gradient calls.

title: What’s the difference between `tf.Variable` and `tf.Tensor` in training loops?
body: Tensor is immutable data container; Variable is mutable, trainable parameter.

title: How do you implement a custom training loop with `train_step`?
body: Write train_step using GradientTape: compute loss, grads, apply via optimizer.

title: What does `model.fit` do under the hood compared to a manual training loop?
body: model.fit automates loop; custom loop gives fine-grained control (GANs, RL).

title: How do you handle class imbalance in TensorFlow/Keras training?
body: Resample, class weights, focal loss, threshold tuning.

title: Explain how to use `tf.data` for performant input pipelines (cache, prefetch, map).
body: Map, shuffle, batch, prefetch, cache, parallel map for performance.

title: What is `AUTOTUNE` in `tf.data` and why use it?
body: AUTOTUNE sets threads/buffers automatically for optimal pipeline parallelism.

title: How do you work with Ragged and Sparse tensors and when are they useful?
body: RaggedTensor: unequal-length sequences; SparseTensor: memory-efficient for mostly zeros.

title: What are distribution strategies and when would you use `MirroredStrategy`?
body: Strategies manage distributed training; MirroredStrategy syncs GPUs on one machine.

title: How do you log training metrics to TensorBoard and visualize them?
body: Use tf.summary to log scalars/images; view in TensorBoard.

title: Explain early stopping and model checkpointing best practices.
body: Callbacks monitoring val_loss/metrics to stop training early or save best model.

title: How do you fine-tune only the top N layers of a pretrained network safely?
body: Set base_model.trainable=False, then unfreeze last N layers and recompile.

title: What is mixed-precision training and how do you enable it?
body: Enable mixed_float16 policy for faster GPU/TPU training with reduced memory use.

title: What are typical steps to avoid data input bottlenecks on GPU training?
body: Use prefetch, parallel_map, cache, data in TFRecords to saturate GPU.

title: How do you export a model for TensorFlow Serving and define signatures?
body: model.save("export"); include signatures; deploy with TF Serving.

title: What is the difference between HDF5 (`.h5`) saves and `SavedModel` format?
body: HDF5 stores only Keras model config/weights; SavedModel stores full TF graph/signatures.

title: How do you load a SavedModel and perform inference efficiently on batches?
body: tf.saved_model.load(path); use signatures["serving_default"](inputs) for batch inference.

title: How do you freeze or serialize a computation graph for deployment?
body: Use tf.compat.v1.graph_util.convert_variables_to_constants, or SavedModel for deployment.

title: What are common causes of shape mismatch errors and how do you debug them?
body: Shape mismatches from wrong batch dims, missing channels; debug via tensor.shape prints.

title: How do you mask padded timesteps in sequence models (RNN/Transformer)?
body: Use mask_zero=True in Embedding, or pass mask argument to layers.

title: What is gradient clipping and why/where would you apply it?
body: Clip gradients by value or norm to prevent exploding gradients.

title: How do you implement learning rate schedules or warmup in Keras?
body: LearningRateScheduler or ExponentialDecay schedules; set in optimizer.

title: Explain how to use `tf.image` or `tf.data` for on-the-fly data augmentation.
body: Use tf.image.random_flip/rotate or Keras preprocessing layers inside dataset.map.

title: How do you test and validate a custom Keras layer or model component?
body: Unit test with dummy inputs, assert output shape/dtype, compare with numpy reference.

title: What’s the difference between training and inference modes in layers like BatchNorm/Dropout?
body: Layers behave differently: dropout off, batchnorm uses moving stats in inference.

title: Design a leakage-free input pipeline with `tf.data` for multi-file, class-imbalanced data at scale.
body: Use tf.data with multiple TFRecord files, class-balanced sampling, shuffle, cache, batch, prefetch.

title: When would you avoid `@tf.function` and stick to eager code despite performance benefits?
body: Debugging ease: eager helps exploration; avoid tf.function for dynamic Python logic not graph-friendly.

title: Explain autograph limitations: which Python constructs don’t convert well to graph?
body: Autograph struggles with dynamic Python features (e.g., complex loops, side-effects, generators).

title: How do you write a numerically stable custom loss using low-level TensorFlow ops?
body: Use numerically stable ops like tf.nn.softmax_cross_entropy_with_logits; avoid direct log/exp.

title: Describe how to implement a custom gradient with `@tf.custom_gradient` and when it’s needed.
body: Decorate function with @tf.custom_gradient; return forward value and custom backward grad.

title: Compare `model.fit` vs fully custom training loop when implementing reinforcement learning or GANs.
body: model.fit hides loop; GANs/RL need manual loop for alternating updates/custom losses.

title: How do you detect and fix silent performance regressions in input pipelines (profiling, tracing)?
body: Profile input pipelines with tf.data.experimental.profiler or TensorBoard trace viewer.

title: Outline a distributed training setup across multiple GPUs and nodes (strategy, collective ops).
body: Use tf.distribute.MirroredStrategy for multi-GPU; MultiWorkerMirrored for multi-node.

title: Explain gradient accumulation in TensorFlow and how to implement it correctly with `GradientTape`.
body: Accumulate grads across steps with GradientTape, then apply once to simulate larger batch.

title: How do you ensure determinism across devices/backends (seeds, ops, cuDNN/threads)?
body: Set seeds, disable nondeterministic ops, set TF_DETERMINISTIC_OPS=1, fix cuDNN versions.

title: Discuss XLA compilation: when to enable it and what pitfalls to watch for.
body: XLA compiles graphs for speed; can break dynamic shapes or custom ops; use with caution.

title: How do you handle very large embeddings (millions of ids) efficiently during training and serving?
body: Use embedding partitioning/sharding, adaptive embeddings, or memory-mapped tables.

title: Design a serving architecture using TensorFlow Serving with versioned `SavedModel`s and A/B traffic.
body: Export versioned SavedModels; configure TF Serving for canary releases, rollbacks.

title: How do you export multiple signatures (preprocess, predict, postprocess) in a single `SavedModel`?

title: What is a network?
body: A network is a group of two or more devices connected to share resources and communicate.

title: What is LAN vs WAN?
body: LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small area (e.g. office), WAN (Wide Area Network) spans larger geographic areas.

title: What is a router?
body: A router forwards packets between different networks using IP routing.

title: What is a switch?
body: A switch connects devices within a LAN and forwards frames based on MAC addresses.

title: What is a hub?
body: A hub is a basic device that broadcasts incoming signals to all ports.

title: What is a firewall?
body: A firewall filters network traffic based on rules to permit or block data.

title: What is an IP address?
body: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network.

title: What is the difference between IPv4 and IPv6?
body: IPv4 uses 32 bits; IPv6 uses 128 bits, offering far more addresses and features.

title: What is a subnet mask?
body: A subnet mask divides an IP address into network and host portions (e.g. 255.255.255.0).

title: What is a default gateway?
body: It is the router interface used to send traffic out of the local network.

title: What is DNS?
body: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names to IP addresses.

title: What is DHCP?
body: DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses and network configuration to devices.

title: What is NAT?
body: NAT (Network Address Translation) allows private IPs to share a public IP and hides internal IPs.

title: What is MAC address?
body: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is a unique hardware identifier at the data link layer.

title: What is ARP?
body: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) maps IP addresses to MAC addresses in a local network.

title: What is a packet?
body: A packet is a unit of data at the network layer, containing headers and payload.

title: What is a frame?
body: A frame is a data link layer unit that encapsulates packets with MAC addressing.

title: What is a port (in networking)?
body: A port is a numerical endpoint for networked services (e.g. TCP port 80 for HTTP).

title: What is TCP?
body: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a reliable, connection-oriented transport protocol.

title: What is UDP?
body: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is connectionless and fast but does not guarantee delivery.

title: What is the three-way handshake (TCP)?
body: The handshake is: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK to establish a connection.

title: What is ping?
body: Ping uses ICMP echo request/reply to check connectivity and round-trip time.

title: What is traceroute?
body: Traceroute finds the path packets take to a destination by listing each hop.

title: What is latency?
body: Latency is the delay for data to travel from source to destination (in ms).

title: What is bandwidth?
body: Bandwidth is the maximum data transfer rate over a network link (e.g. Mbps).

title: What is throughput?
body: Throughput is the actual achieved data transfer rate over a period, considering overhead.

title: What is jitter?
body: Jitter is the variation in latency between packets.

title: What is packet loss?
body: Packet loss is when packets fail to reach the destination (dropped or corrupted).

title: What is collision domain?
body: A collision domain is a network segment where packet collisions can occur (in Ethernet).

title: What is broadcast domain?
body: A broadcast domain is a network area where broadcast frames are propagated.

title: What is CIDR notation (e.g. /24)?
body: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) expresses IP subnetting by prefix length (e.g. /24 means 255.255.255.0, 24 bits network).

title: How many usable hosts are there in a /28 network?
body: In a /28, 16 total addresses, 14 usable hosts (2 reserved for network & broadcast).

title: What is classful IP addressing?
body: Classful addressing divides IP space into fixed classes (A, B, C, D, E) by first octet.

title: What is loopback address?
body: The loopback address (127.0.0.1 in IPv4) refers to the local host itself.

title: What is APIPA / Link-local address?
body: APIPA (169.254.x.x) or IPv6 link-local (fe80::/10) used when DHCP fails.

title: Explain the OSI model’s 7 layers.
body: List from bottom: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application — with roles.

title: Which OSI layers correspond to TCP/IP model?
body: Application, Transport, Internet (Network), Network Access (Link + Physical).

title: What is the difference between switch and bridge?
body: A bridge connects two network segments at layer 2; a switch is multiport bridge handling many segments.

title: What is STP (Spanning Tree Protocol)?
body: STP prevents loops in a bridged Ethernet network by disabling redundant paths.

title: What is a MAC table / CAM table?
body: A switch’s table mapping MAC addresses to switch ports.

title: What is ARP spoofing?
body: ARP spoofing is a malicious attack sending fake ARP messages to associate attacker’s MAC with another IP.

title: What is port forwarding?
body: Forwarding external traffic on a port to an internal host in NAT.

title: What is DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) in network?
body: A DMZ is an isolated subnet that exposes public services while protecting internal network.

title: What is load balancing?
body: Distributing network traffic across multiple servers to improve performance and availability.

title: What is link aggregation / LACP?
body: Combining multiple network links into a single logical link for higher bandwidth / redundancy.

title: What is QoS (Quality of Service)?
body: QoS is controlling traffic priority to ensure reliable performance (e.g. for VoIP).

title: What is MPLS?
body: Multiprotocol Label Switching — forwarding based on labels rather than IP addresses, for traffic engineering.

title: What is BGP (Border Gateway Protocol)?
body: BGP is the routing protocol between autonomous systems on the Internet.

title: What is OSPF?
body: Open Shortest Path First — internal routing protocol that uses link-state algorithm within an AS.

title: What is EIGRP?
body: EIGRP is a Cisco-proprietary hybrid routing protocol combining distance-vector and link-state features.

title: What is RIP?
body: Routing Information Protocol — distance-vector routing protocol with hop count metric.

title: What is route redistribution?
body: Route redistribution allows sharing routing info between different routing protocols.

title: What is asymmetric routing?
body: Traffic uses different paths for outbound and inbound directions.

title: What is ICMP?
body: Internet Control Message Protocol — used for network diagnostics (e.g. ping, traceroute).

title: What is MTU?
body: Maximum Transmission Unit — the largest packet size that can be transmitted over a network link.

title: What is fragmentation?
body: Breaking large IP packets into smaller ones to fit MTU sizes.

title: What is TTL (Time to Live)?
body: TTL limits packet lifetime (in hops) to avoid routing loops.

title: What is NAT types (SNAT, DNAT, PAT)?
body: SNAT (source NAT), DNAT (destination NAT), PAT (port address translation).

title: What is a proxy server?
body: A proxy acts as an intermediary between clients and servers, filtering or caching requests.

title: What is a tunneling protocol?
body: Protocol encapsulating packets inside another protocol (e.g. GRE, IPsec tunnel).

title: Explain how TCP flow control works (sliding window).
body: TCP uses a window size advertised by receiver; sender can send only that much unacknowledged data; window changes dynamically.

title: Explain TCP congestion control (slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, fast recovery).
body: TCP starts slow (slow start), increases until threshold, then linear growth (congestion avoidance). On packet loss, retranmsmit fast or reduce window (fast retransmit / recovery).

title: What is BGP route selection process (attributes)?
body: BGP path selection uses attributes: Weight, Local Preference, AS Path, Origin, MED, eBGP over iBGP, shortest IGP path, etc.

title: What is route flapping?
body: Route flapping is frequent changes of route up/down, causing instability.

title: How does OSPF compute shortest path (Dijkstra)?
body: OSPF uses link-state algorithm: each router builds complete map and runs Dijkstra’s algorithm to compute best paths.

title: What are OSPF LSA types (1–5)?
body: LSA type 1 (router), 2 (network), 3 (summary), 4 (ASBR), 5 (external) for OSPFv2 (plus others in OSPFv3).

title: What is MPLS TE (Traffic Engineering)?
body: MPLS TE guides traffic along non-default paths using RSVP-TE, constraints, and explicit routes.

title: Explain SDN (Software Defined Networking).
body: SDN decouples control plane from data plane; centralized controller programs forwarding devices via APIs.

title: What is VXLAN?
body: Virtual Extensible LAN — encapsulates layer-2 frames in UDP for overlay networks in data centers.

title: What is NAT traversal (e.g. STUN, TURN)?
body: NAT traversal techniques permit communication across NAT, e.g. STUN, TURN, ICE in VoIP.

title: What is DWDM?
body: Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing — optical tech to send multiple wavelengths on fiber.

title: What is MPLS LSP?
body: An MPLS Label Switched Path — a precomputed path that packets follow using labels.

title: Explain segment routing in networking.
body: Segment routing encodes path as sequence of segments, reducing state in core network.

title: What is TEAS (Traffic Engineering Architecture and Signaling)?
body: TEAS is a framework under IETF for traffic engineering signaling, path control, etc.

title: What is RSVP-TE?
body: Resource Reservation Protocol (Traffic Engineering) — reserves resources along a path in MPLS TE.

title: Explain MPLS Fast Reroute.
body: Fast Reroute provides precomputed backup paths to reroute traffic quickly upon failure.

title: Explain link-state vs distance-vector routing protocols.
body: Link-state: routers exchange full topology, compute shortest path (e.g. OSPF). Distance-vector: routers exchange routing tables (e.g. RIP), count hops.

title: What is IS-IS?
body: Intermediate System to Intermediate System — link-state routing protocol used in large networks.

title: What is BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection)?
body: BFD is a fast detection protocol to detect link failures in sub-second time.

title: What is an operating system?
body: A software layer that manages hardware & software resources and provides services to applications and users.

title: Name three functions of an OS.
body: Process management, memory management, file system management.

title: What is a process?
body: A program in execution with its own memory space and resources.

title: What is kernel?
body: The core component of an OS that has full control over hardware and runs in privileged mode.

title: What is user mode vs kernel mode?
body: User mode is restricted with limited privileges; kernel mode has full privileges.

title: What is paging?
body: A memory management scheme dividing memory into fixed size blocks (“pages”) which map virtual memory to physical memory.

title: What is swapping?
body: Moving processes or data between main memory and secondary storage (disk) to free memory.

title: What is context switch?
body: Saving state of one process/thread and loading the state of another to switch execution.

title: Name two CPU scheduling algorithms.

title: What is FCFS scheduling?
body: Processes are scheduled in the order they arrive.

title: What is Round Robin scheduling?
body: Each process is assigned a fixed time slice in cyclic order.

title: What is priority scheduling?
body: Processes are scheduled based on priority; higher priority gets CPU first.

title: What is starvation?
body: When low priority processes never get CPU time because high priority processes keep preempting them.

title: What is aging (in scheduling)?
body: Increasing priority of waiting processes over time to prevent starvation.

title: What is deadlock?
body: A situation where two or more processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.

title: What are the necessary conditions for deadlock?
body: Mutual exclusion, hold & wait, no preemption, circular wait.

title: What is file system?
body: A system for storing and retrieving files on storage devices.

title: What is directory?
body: A special file that contains listings of files and/or other directories.

title: What is input/output management in OS?
body: Managing and coordinating communication between computer and peripherals.

title: What is interrupt?

body: The sequence of operations from power on to loading the OS kernel.

title: What is device driver?
body: Software that acts as translator between OS and hardware device.

title: What is memory fragmentation?

title: What is logical address vs physical address?
body: Logical address is used by program; physical address is actual address in RAM.

title: What is page fault?
body: When a program accesses a page not currently in memory causing OS to load it.

title: Explain the difference between internal and external fragmentation.

title: What is segmentation?
body: Dividing a program’s memory into logical segments (e.g., code, data, stack).

title: What is the purpose of swap space?
body: Holds contents of memory pages that are not actively used to free RAM.

title: What are system threads vs user threads?

title: What is multiprogramming?
body: Running multiple programs concurrently by sharing CPU time and other resources.

title: What is multitasking vs multiprocessing?

title: What is preemptive scheduling?
body: OS can interrupt a running process to schedule another.

title: What is non-preemptive scheduling?
body: Process runs until it blocks or finishes.

title: What is I/O scheduling?
body: Ordering and controlling how I/O operations are submitted to devices to improve performance.

title: What are the differences among file allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed)?
body: Contiguous: files stored in contiguous blocks; linked: blocks linked list; indexed: using an index block for pointers.

title: What is RAID and give an example level?
body: RAID is Redundant Array of Independent Disks; e.g., RAID-1 mirrors data across disks.

title: What is swapping vs paging?
body: Swapping moves whole processes; paging moves only fixed-sized pages.

title: What is kernel preemption?
body: Kernel allows interrupting of currently running process in kernel mode to schedule another.

title: What is operating system bootloader?
body: A small program that loads the OS kernel into memory during startup.

title: What is mutual exclusion?
body: A property that ensures only one process at a time can execute a critical section.

title: What is a mutex vs semaphore?
body: Mutex is a lock for mutual exclusion; semaphore is more general synchronization primitive.

title: What is producer-consumer problem?
body: A synchronization problem where a producer produces data for consumer to consume, requiring coordination.

title: What is critical section?
body: Part of code where shared resource is accessed and must not be concurrently accessed by multiple threads.

title: What is synchronization?
body: Ensuring correct sequencing among threads or processes when accessing shared data.

title: What is barrier synchronization?
body: Ensures that multiple threads reach a certain point before any can proceed.

title: What is priority inversion?
body: When lower-priority task holds resource needed by higher-priority task, blocking it.

title: What are kernel modules?
body: Code that can be loaded or unloaded into kernel at runtime to extend functionality without reboot.

title: What is the difference between monolithic vs microkernel OS architecture?
body: Monolithic: most services in kernel; microkernel: minimal kernel, services run in user space.

title: What is virtual file system (VFS)?
body: An abstraction layer allowing multiple file system types to be accessed uniformly.

title: What is device management?
body: Managing device drivers, buffering, caching, and communication with I/O devices.

title: What is disk scheduling algorithms (e.g., SSTF, SCAN)?
body: Algorithms to order disk I/O requests to reduce seek time.

title: What is real-time operating system?
body: OS that guarantees response within strict time constraints.

title: What is a thread pool?
body: Collection of threads to serve multiple tasks without frequent creation/destroy overhead.

title: Explain how virtual memory is implemented using page tables.
body: Page tables map virtual pages to physical frames; include multi-level page tables or inverted page tables to manage memory efficiently.

title: What is TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer)?
body: A cache of recent page table entries to accelerate address translation.

title: What is hierarchical paging?
body: Paging using multiple levels of page tables, reducing memory overhead.

title: Explain page replacement algorithms (LRU, FIFO, Optimal).
body: Algorithms decide which page to evict when new page is loaded; LRU evicts least recently used; FIFO evicts oldest; Optimal minimizes future faults.

title: What are system calls and how are they implemented?
body: User-mode program invokes special instruction/trap, switches to kernel, executes service, returns to user mode.

title: Explain deadlock detection vs avoidance vs prevention.

title: What is Banker's algorithm?

title: Explain what semaphores are and differences with spinlocks.
body: Semaphores block when waiting; spinlocks busy-wait; spinlocks better for short critical sections.

title: What is priority inversion problem & how OS solves it (e.g., priority inheritance)?

title: Explain kernel preemption challenges.
body: In concurrency, preempting kernel code needs careful synchronization and may introduce complexity/race conditions.

title: What is memory mapped I/O vs port-mapped I/O?

title: Explain swapping vs paging vs segmentation.
body: Differences in how memory is divided and managed.

title: How do OSs ensure protection between processes?
body: Using memory protection, user vs kernel modes, access permissions, hardware features (MMU).

title: What is address space layout randomization (ASLR)?
body: Security technique randomizing memory addresses to prevent exploit predictability.

title: Explain secure boot process.

title: What is operating system journaling in file systems?

title: What are capabilities of modern OS in terms of sandboxing?

title: What is memory leak?

title: What is paging vs segmentation trade-offs?

title: What is cryptography?

title: What is a cipher?

title: What is a key?
body: A piece of information used by a cryptographic algorithm to encrypt or decrypt.

title: What is a secret key?
body: In symmetric encryption, the shared key known only to communicating parties.

title: What is hashing?
body: Turning input data into fixed-length digest; non-reversible.

title: What is MD5?

title: What is SHA-1?
body: Secure Hash Algorithm 1, older and weaker than SHA-2; collision prone.

title: What is SHA-256?
body: SHA-2 variant with 256-bit hash; widely used today.

title: What is HMAC?
body: Hash-based Message Authentication Code; hash plus secret key to verify integrity and authenticity.

title: What is salt in hashing?
body: Random data added to input before hashing to prevent rainbow table attacks.

title: What is key exchange?
body: Method for two parties to share cryptographic keys securely.

title: What is Diffie-Hellman?
body: A key exchange algorithm allowing two parties to agree on a shared secret over an insecure channel.

title: What is AES?
body: Advanced Encryption Standard; symmetric cipher widely used.

title: What is DES?
body: Older symmetric cipher; largely deprecated due to vulnerabilities.

title: What is Triple DES (3DES)?
body: Applying DES three times for increased security.

title: What is RSA?
body: Asymmetric algorithm used for encryption and signatures.

title: What is ECC?
body: Elliptic Curve Cryptography; asymmetric method providing strong security with smaller keys.

title: What is block cipher?
body: Processes fixed-size blocks of plaintext, e.g., AES.

title: What is stream cipher?
body: Encrypts plaintext one bit or byte at a time, e.g. RC4 (though weak).

title: What is cipher mode (CBC, ECB)?
body: Methods how to apply block cipher to larger data; ECB insecure, CBC uses chaining.

title: What is initialization vector (IV)?
body: Random or pseudo-random value used to ensure different ciphertexts.

title: What is symmetric key length importance?
body: Short keys are easier to brute-force; longer keys offer better security.

title: What is public key infrastructure (PKI)?
body: Framework for managing keys, certificates, and trust.

title: What is padding in encryption?
body: Adding extra data so plaintext fits block size requirements.

title: What is PKCS#7 padding?
body: A padding standard for block ciphers.

title: What is OAEP used with RSA?
body: Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding used to mitigate RSA’s padding attacks.

title: What is key derivation function (KDF)?

title: What is PBKDF2?
body: Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2; slows brute force via many iterations.

title: What is bcrypt?
body: Key stretching algorithm designed for password hashing.

title: What is scrypt?
body: KDF emphasizing memory hardness to resist GPU attacks.

title: What is Argon2?
body: KDF winner of password hashing competition with memory-hard properties.

title: What is perfect forward secrecy (PFS)?

title: What is digital certificate?

title: What is CRL vs OCSP?

body: Encryption that provides both confidentiality and integrity checks.

title: What is side-channel attack?

title: What is padding oracle attack?
body: Exploiting decryption error responses to reveal plaintext.

title: What is man-in-the-middle attack in key exchange?

title: What is elliptical curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH)?

title: What is SHA-3?
body: Newer hash algorithm standard with sponge construction design.

body: Block cipher mode offering confidentiality, integrity, and authentication.

title: What is nonce?
body: A number used once to ensure encryption randomness and prevent replay.

title: What is symmetric key distribution problem?
body: Challenge of securely sharing the same key between parties.

title: What is hybrid encryption?
body: Combination of symmetric (for speed) and asymmetric (for secure key exchange).

title: What is MAC (Message Authentication Code)?
body: Code ensuring message integrity and authenticity.

title: What is homomorphic encryption?
body: Encryption allowing computation on ciphertext without decrypting.

title: What is threshold cryptography?
body: Distributing key operations so multiple parties must cooperate to decrypt or sign.

title: What is lattice-based cryptography?
body: Cryptography based on hard lattice problems; candidate for post-quantum security.

title: What is post-quantum cryptography?
body: Cryptographic techniques resistant to quantum computer attacks.

body: Advanced ECC operations used in some advanced crypto protocols.

title: What is oblivious transfer?

title: What does DNS stand for?
body: Domain Name System - translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses that computers use to identify each other.

title: What is the primary function of DNS?
body: Resolves domain names to IP addresses allowing users to access websites using memorable names instead of numeric IP addresses.

title: Which port does DNS typically use?
body: Port 53 for both UDP (queries) and TCP (zone transfers and large responses).

title: What is a DNS A record?
body: Maps a domain name to an IPv4 address (32-bit) enabling browsers to locate web servers.

title: What is a DNS AAAA record?
body: Maps a domain name to an IPv6 address (128-bit) for next-generation internet protocol.

title: What is DNS caching?
body: Temporary storage of DNS query results to reduce lookup time and network traffic for frequently accessed domains.

title: What does TTL mean in DNS?
body: Time To Live - specifies how long (in seconds) a DNS record should be cached before requesting fresh data.

title: What is a DNS root server?
body: Top-level servers in the DNS hierarchy that direct queries to appropriate TLD (Top Level Domain) servers.

title: What is a DNS resolver?
body: Client-side component or server that initiates DNS queries on behalf of applications and caches responses.

title: What is a DNS zone?
body: Administrative space or portion of the DNS namespace managed by specific organization or administrator.

title: What is an MX record?
body: Mail Exchange record that specifies mail servers responsible for accepting email on behalf of a domain.

title: What is a CNAME record?
body: Canonical Name record that creates an alias pointing one domain name to another domain name.

title: What is a PTR record?
body: Pointer record used for reverse DNS lookups mapping IP addresses back to domain names.

title: What is an NS record?
body: Name Server record that delegates a DNS zone to use specific authoritative name servers.

title: What is a TXT record?
body: Text record that holds arbitrary text data often used for domain verification and email security policies.

title: What is DNS propagation?
body: Time it takes for DNS changes to update across all servers worldwide typically 24-48 hours.

title: What is a DNS query?
body: Request sent by a client to a DNS server asking for the IP address associated with a domain name.

title: What is a forward DNS lookup?
body: Translating a domain name into its corresponding IP address the most common DNS operation.

title: What is a reverse DNS lookup?
body: Translating an IP address back into its associated domain name using PTR records.

title: What is a recursive DNS query?
body: Query where DNS server takes full responsibility for finding the answer and returns final result to client.

title: What is an iterative DNS query?
body: Query where DNS server returns best answer it has or referral to another server for client to query next.

title: What is a DNS server?
body: Computer server that contains a database of public IP addresses and their associated domain names.

title: What is DNS hierarchy?
body: Tree-like structure with root servers at top followed by TLD servers and authoritative name servers.

title: What is a primary DNS server?
body: Main DNS server that holds the original read-write copies of zone data.

title: What is a secondary DNS server?
body: Backup DNS server that holds read-only copies of zone data transferred from primary server.

title: What is a DNS forwarder?
body: DNS server that forwards queries it cannot resolve to another DNS server for resolution.

title: What is a DNS zone file?
body: Text file that contains mappings between domain names and IP addresses for a DNS zone.

title: What is an SOA record?
body: Start of Authority record containing administrative information about DNS zone including primary name server.

title: What is DNS resolution?
body: Complete process of converting a domain name into an IP address through DNS queries.

title: What is a DNS client?
body: Any device or application that initiates DNS queries to resolve domain names typically end-user devices.

title: What is DNS cache poisoning?
body: Attack where false DNS data is inserted into DNS resolver cache causing it to return incorrect IP addresses and redirect users to malicious sites.

title: What is the difference between authoritative and non-authoritative DNS responses?
body: Authoritative comes from server with original zone data non-authoritative comes from cached data on resolver.

title: What is DNS amplification attack?
body: DDoS attack exploiting open DNS resolvers by sending small queries with spoofed source IP causing large responses to flood victim.

title: What is split-horizon DNS?
body: Configuration providing different DNS responses based on whether query originates from internal or external network.

title: What is DNS load balancing?
body: Using multiple A records with different IP addresses for same domain allowing distribution of traffic across servers.

title: What is a DNS glue record?
body: A record in parent zone providing IP address of name server in child zone to prevent circular dependencies.

title: What is DNS failover?
body: Automatic redirection of traffic to backup servers when primary server fails detected through health checks.

title: What is a Git branch?

title: What is Maven?
body: Build automation and dependency management tool primarily for Java projects using XML configuration (pom.xml).

title: What is pom.xml?
body: Project Object Model file containing project configuration dependencies plugins and build settings for Maven.

title: What is a Maven dependency?
body: External library or project that your project requires declared in pom.xml for automatic download.

title: What is Maven Central Repository?
body: Default remote repository hosting open-source Java libraries and artifacts for Maven projects.

title: What does 'mvn clean' do?
body: Deletes the target directory removing all compiled classes and build artifacts starting fresh build.

title: What does 'mvn compile' do?
body: Compiles source code in src/main/java directory producing class files in target/classes.

title: What does 'mvn test' do?
body: Compiles and executes unit tests in src/test/java directory generating test reports.

title: What does 'mvn package' do?
body: Creates distributable format like JAR or WAR file from compiled code and resources.

title: What does 'mvn install' do?
body: Installs packaged artifact into local Maven repository for use by other local projects.

title: What is Maven lifecycle?
body: Predefined sequence of phases representing different stages of project build process.

title: What is a Maven plugin?
body: Component extending Maven functionality providing additional goals for various build tasks.

title: What is Maven local repository?
body: Directory on local machine (~/.m2/repository) where Maven stores downloaded dependencies and built artifacts.

title: What is groupId in Maven?
body: Unique identifier for organization or group creating the project usually reverse domain name.

title: What is artifactId in Maven?
body: Name of the project or module being built serving as unique identifier within group.

title: What is version in Maven?
body: Release version of artifact following semantic versioning with SNAPSHOT indicating development version.

title: What is Maven goal?
body: Specific task that can be executed like compile test or package representing unit of work.

title: What is Maven phase?
body: Stage in build lifecycle where plugins goals are executed in defined sequence.

title: What is src/main/java directory?
body: Standard location for application source code in Maven project structure.

title: What is src/test/java directory?
body: Standard location for test code in Maven project structure.

title: What is target directory?
body: Output directory where Maven places compiled classes packaged artifacts and generated files.

title: What is a Maven archetype?
body: Project template providing structure and basic configuration for new Maven projects.

title: What does 'mvn clean install' do?
body: Removes old builds compiles tests packages and installs artifact in local repository in one command.

title: What is Maven's convention over configuration?
body: Principle providing sensible defaults reducing configuration needed for standard project structures.

title: What is a JAR file in Maven?
body: Java Archive file containing compiled classes and resources packaged by Maven.

title: What is a WAR file in Maven?
body: Web Application Archive containing web application components like servlets JSPs and configuration files.

title: What is Maven scope?
body: Defines visibility and classpath availability of dependency like compile test or provided.

title: What is the default Maven lifecycle?
body: Clean validate compile test package verify install deploy representing complete build process.

title: What is settings.xml in Maven?
body: Configuration file for Maven installation containing repository credentials mirrors and profiles.

title: What does 'mvn deploy' do?
body: Uploads built artifact to remote repository for sharing with other developers or projects.

title: What is Maven wrapper?
body: Script allowing project to use specific Maven version without requiring global installation.

title: What is transitive dependency in Maven?
body: Dependencies of your dependencies automatically included by Maven requiring careful management.

title: What is dependency management section?
body: POM section defining versions of dependencies for entire project or multi-module build for consistency.

title: What is Maven profile?
body: Named configuration variant allowing different build behaviors for different environments or conditions.

title: What is dependency scope compile?
body: Default scope making dependency available in all classpaths including compilation test and runtime.

title: What is dependency scope provided?
body: Indicates dependency supplied by runtime environment like servlet API provided by application server.

title: What is dependency scope test?
body: Limits dependency to test compilation and execution not included in final artifact.

title: What is dependency scope runtime?
body: Dependency not needed for compilation but required during execution and testing.

title: What is Maven multi-module project?
body: Project containing multiple related modules with parent POM managing common configuration.

title: What is parent POM?
body: POM file containing shared configuration for child modules enabling inheritance and centralized management.

title: What is dependency exclusion?
body: Mechanism to prevent specific transitive dependencies from being included resolving conflicts.

title: What is Maven plugin configuration?
body: XML defining how plugin behaves including parameters execution goals and phase binding.

title: What is Maven repository manager?
body: Server like Nexus or Artifactory caching artifacts and hosting private dependencies for organization.

title: What is SNAPSHOT version?
body: Development version that can be updated indicating work in progress before final release.

title: What is Maven release plugin?
body: Tool automating release process including version updates tagging and deployment to repository.

title: What is Maven Surefire plugin?
body: Plugin executing unit tests during test phase generating reports and failing build on test failures.

title: What is Maven compiler plugin?
body: Configures Java compiler version and compilation options for source and target compatibility.

title: What is effective POM?
body: Complete POM after inheritance aggregation and interpolation showing all configuration Maven uses.

title: What is Maven properties?
body: Variables defined in POM for reuse throughout configuration reducing duplication.

title: What is Maven dependency tree?
body: Hierarchical view showing all dependencies and their transitive dependencies for conflict analysis.

title: What is version range in Maven?
body: Specification allowing flexible dependency versions using brackets and parentheses for min/max versions.

title: What is Maven assembly plugin?
body: Creates custom distribution packages combining project output dependencies and resources.

title: What is Maven enforcer plugin?
body: Validates project conforms to rules like dependency convergence required Java version and banned dependencies.

title: What is Maven resources plugin?
body: Copies project resources to output directory with filtering for variable substitution.

title: What is Maven jar plugin?
body: Configures JAR file creation including manifest entries and included/excluded files.

title: What is build helper plugin?
body: Provides additional build lifecycle goals like adding extra source directories or attaching artifacts.

title: What is Maven failsafe plugin?
body: Executes integration tests in separate lifecycle phase with different failure handling than Surefire.

title: What is dependency mediation in Maven?
body: Resolution strategy when multiple versions exist choosing nearest in dependency tree or first declared.

title: What is Maven artifact repository?
body: Location storing versioned artifacts can be local remote or repository manager.

title: What is Maven mirror configuration?
body: Redirecting repository requests to alternative location for faster access or organizational policy.

title: How to resolve complex dependency conflicts in Maven?
body: Use dependency:tree analyze mediation rules explicitly declare versions use dependency management and exclude conflicting transitives.

title: What is Maven's dependency resolution algorithm?
body: Nearest wins strategy with first declaration tiebreaker using depth-first traversal of dependency tree for conflict resolution.

title: How to optimize Maven build performance?
body: Use parallel builds incremental compilation dependency caching optimize plugin configuration and use repository manager.

title: What is Maven's build lifecycle internals?
body: Three lifecycles (clean default site) with phases bound to plugins goals executed sequentially during build.

title: How to implement custom Maven plugin?
body: Extend AbstractMojo implement execute method define parameters use annotations and package as Maven plugin artifact.

title: What is Maven's POM inheritance model?
body: Four-level model - super POM parent POM project POM and effective POM with merging and override rules.

title: How to handle circular dependencies in Maven?
body: Redesign module structure extract common code use dependency management or consider build reactor ordering issues.

title: What is Maven's integration with CI/CD?
body: Standardized build commands artifact deployment integration with Jenkins GitLab CI and version management automation.

title: How to implement Maven release management?
body: Use release plugin semantic versioning SCM integration automated testing staging repository and rollback procedures.

title: What is Maven's approach to handling large monorepos?
body: Multi-module builds incremental builds parallel execution selective reactor and consider performance implications.

title: How to implement Maven for microservices?
body: Parent POM for shared configuration individual modules for services dependency management and containerization integration.

title: What is Maven's plugin development architecture?
body: Mojo API parameter injection lifecycle integration plugin testing and repository deployment for distribution.

title: How to troubleshoot Maven dependency hell?
body: Analyze dependency tree use enforcer plugin understand mediation rules explicit versions and repository inspection.

title: What is Maven's repository layout and metadata?
body: Standard directory structure with Maven metadata XML files SHA checksums and repository index for searching.

title: How to implement custom Maven lifecycle?
body: Create lifecycle mapping define phases bind plugins configure in META-INF/plexus and package as extension.

title: What is Maven's approach to version management?
body: Semantic versioning SNAPSHOT handling version properties dependency management and automated version updates.

title: How to secure Maven builds and dependencies?
body: Verify checksums use repository managers scan vulnerabilities use HTTPS implement access control and audit dependencies.

title: What is Maven's memory and performance tuning?
body: Configure MAVEN_OPTS heap size parallel builds fork mode and optimize plugin execution for large projects.

title: How to implement Maven archetype development?
body: Create archetype project define archetype-metadata descriptor use velocity templates test archetype and deploy to repository.

title: What is Maven's extension mechanism?
body: Components loaded before build starts modify core behavior provide custom lifecycle or enhance repository access
